item.title: Bisectors in the Heisenberg group II
item.description: arXiv:2610.13954v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Following previous work on metric bisectors with respect to the Kor\'anyi metric, we study here bisectors in the Heisenberg group $\mathfrak{H}$ equipped with the Carnot--Carath\'eodory metric $d_{cc}$.
item.dc:creator: Gaoshun Gou, Joonhyung Kim, Ioannis D. Platis, Li-Jie Sun

item.title: Equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations on Hermitian symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.14045v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate and solve a $G$-equivariant analogue of the Seiberg-Witten equations on any irreducible Hermitian symmetric space $G/K$. We use a canonical $K$-invariant form to define a twisted Hodge operator generalising self-duality to higher dimensions. The resulting equivariant Seiberg-Witten equations arise, for a compact $G/K$, as conditions for the absolute minima of an energy functional. Their linear part has a representation theoretic interpretation: the same Weyl group data control the highest-weight realisation of the positive Dirac kernel in the compact case and its discrete-series realisation on the non-compact dual. This space of harmonic spinors collapses almost entirely by the quadratic conditions of the monopole equation. In the compact case, the equivariant moduli set, when non-empty, is a single gauge class, identifying with the $G$-invariant part of Bradlow's trichotomy for vortices, while in the non-compact case, every irreducible solution sits outside the discrete series.
item.dc:creator: Rafailia-Persefoni Tsiavou

item.title: A Proof of the Analytic Entropy Conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.14065v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that the geodesic flow of a closed real-analytic Riemannian manifold has zero topological entropy if it admits globally defined, real-analytic Liouville integrals. This proves a longstanding conjecture proposed by Bolsinov and Taimanov.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoyang Chen, Xiang Jiang

item.title: An Explicit Bound for the First Dirichlet Eigenvalue via Two Moments
item.description: arXiv:2610.14069v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^n,g)$, $n\ge2$, be a compact connected Riemannian manifold with smooth nonempty boundary, $\operatorname{Ric}_M\ge(n-1)Kg$ for $K>0$, and nonnegative outward boundary mean curvature. We derive an explicit algebraic lower bound $B_\eta$ for the first Dirichlet eigenvalue from Kasue's mixed inradius model. With $R$ the inradius and $s=4KR^2/\pi^2$, the bound involves one square root and approximates the model eigenvalue with relative error $O_n(s^4)$ as $s\downarrow0$ for fixed $n$. The construction uses the first two moments of a positive representation of the averaged model potential and a sharp pointwise corrector estimate. For the chosen spectral transfer, the first two moments determine an optimal bound. We also show that the model eigenvalue is the geometric infimum at fixed $(n,K,R)$. For $0<s<1$, it is approached by smooth collapsing balls with sectional curvature at least $K$ and totally geodesic boundary. At the maximal inradius, the model value is attained by the round hemisphere. The bound strictly improves the variance refinement throughout $0<s\le1$. We also give a direct algebraic comparison with an optimized power-test benchmark.
item.dc:creator: Thomas Sch\"urmann

item.title: Distinguished bases and the braid group action for solutions of the tt*-Toda equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.14078v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We implement (in a concrete example) a procedure of Dubrovin which gives a braid group action on spaces of solutions of ordinary differential equations such as the quantum differential equation of complex projective space. Such actions originated in physics for the tt* (topological-antitopological fusion) equations. We make the procedure systematic by utilizing an algebraic description of braid group actions on distinguished bases. We also generalize to the case of (arbitrary) solutions of the tt*-Toda equations, one of which corresponds to the quantum cohomology of complex projective space.
item.dc:creator: Yudai Hateruma

item.title: An Abresch-Rosenberg type tensor and a gap theorem for CMC hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.14223v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a symmetric trace-free tensor for constant-mean-curvature hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ that extends the Abresch-Rosenberg tensor. Within its natural class, it is characterized by the linearity of its Codazzi defect, and its complete connected zero set consists exactly of the rotational CMC spheres. An exact integrated Simons identity yields explicit gap theorems, valid for every $h>1$ in $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ and every $h>(n\int_0^{\pi/2}\sin^{n-1}r\,dr)^{-1}$ in $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$. We compare the pinching thresholds with the pointwise algebraic level that implies convexity. In $\mathbb{H}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ the explicit pinching conditions imply strict convexity, so there the method gives an independent proof with explicit constants. In $\mathbb{S}^n\times\mathbb{R}$ the pinching region exceeds the convexity level for $n\in\{3,4\}$ and every admissible $h$, and for $n\geq5$ whenever $h^2\geq n/(6(n+2))$; there the gap theorem does not require convexity to be known in advance. We also determine second-order large-$h$ asymptotics of the thresholds.
item.dc:creator: Hil\'ario Alencar, M\'arcio Batista, Harold Rosenberg

item.title: Asymptotically conical shrinking ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow: rotational construction and uniqueness
item.description: arXiv:2610.14227v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For $1\leq r\leq n-1$ we study shrinking self-similar ends of the $r$-mean curvature flow, $S_r=c\langle X,N\rangle$ with $c<0$, that are asymptotic to a cone. For every rotational cone of positive slope we construct a smooth embedded rotational end and prove that its profile is the only positive solution of the profile equation with the prescribed slope at infinity. Its angular defect $xu'-u$ is strictly negative, which yields $r$-admissibility, and the profile has a complete asymptotic expansion for $u(x)/x$ in powers of $x^{-(r+1)}$, valid after arbitrary differentiation. The profiles depend real analytically on the slope and, on sufficiently distant exterior regions, foliate the image of the corresponding family. Our main result removes the symmetry assumption: two ends that converge smoothly, with multiplicity one, to the same circular cone coincide outside a compact set. The proof transforms the equation for their difference into an almost-eigenfunction inequality for a drift Laplacian on an auxiliary conical metric and applies Bernstein's asymptotic analysis on weakly conical ends. The argument extends to strictly $r$-admissible cones whose links have constant principal curvatures.
item.dc:creator: Hil\'ario Alencar, M\'arcio Batista, Greg\'orio Silva Neto

item.title: Inner and outer isometries of graphs of polynomials
item.description: arXiv:2610.14291v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We classify graphs of complex polynomials in one variable up to isometry, both for the inner (length) distance and for the outer (Euclidean) distance of $\mathbb{C}^2\cong\mathbb{R}^4$. For polynomials $p,q$ with $\deg p\ge 2$ we show that the graphs of $p$ and $q$ are inner isometric if and only if they are outer isometric, if and only if $p(z)=\alpha\,q(\beta z+h)+k$ or $p(z)=\alpha\,\bar q(\beta z+h)+k$ for some $\alpha,\beta,h,k\in\mathbb{C}$ with $|\alpha|=|\beta|=1$, where $\bar q$ denotes the polynomial with conjugate coefficients. Moreover, every inner isometry between such graphs is the restriction of an isometry of $\mathbb{C}^2$; in this sense graphs of complex polynomials are isometrically rigid. We contrast this with the real case, where the two distances behave very differently: the graphs of any two real polynomials are inner isometric, whereas, for degree at least $2$, outer isometries are generated by translations, reflections in horizontal and vertical lines and half-turns.
item.dc:creator: Alexandre Fernandes, Claudia Fernandes, Edson Sampaio

item.title: The Height of Choe's Higher-Dimensional Enneper Surface
item.description: arXiv:2610.14343v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that Choe's higher-dimensional Enneper hypersurfaces in $\mathbb R^{n+1}$, $3\le n\le6$, cannot be confined between two parallel hyperplanes, disproving his slab confinement conjecture. We further strengthen this conclusion by determining their precise height growth exponent. If $H(R)$ denotes the maximal absolute height above the asymptotic hyperplane within the horizontal ball of radius $R$, then $H(R)=R^{\alpha_1+o(1)}$ as $R\to\infty$, where $\alpha_1=\frac{\sqrt{(n-2)^2+4\lambda_1(\Omega)}-(n-2)}{2}$, $\Omega=S^{n-1}\setminus[0,\infty)^n$, and $\lambda_1(\Omega)$ is the first Dirichlet eigenvalue of the spherical Laplacian. In particular, $0<\alpha_1<1$, so the height is unbounded but grows sublinearly. The proof combines the blow-down behavior of a fundamental piece of Choe's hypersurface with the rigidity of positive harmonic functions on cones. In dimension two, the formula gives $2/3$, recovering the classical Enneper height-growth exponent.
item.dc:creator: Yike He

item.title: Volume growth and parabolicity for non-symmetric operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.14375v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The interplay between a weighted volume measure and its naturally associated weighted Laplace operator is fundamental to the geometric analysis of weighted structures governed by gradient vector fields. Beyond the gradient setting, however, the theory has remained considerably less developed, largely because this natural correspondence is lost. In this paper, we identify invariant measures as the appropriate framework for extending the theory to general drifted Laplace operators. This approach yields a systematic treatment of parabolicity in the non-gradient setting, reveals its connection with volume growth, and leads to new volume finiteness results for non-gradient geometric structures.
item.dc:creator: Leandro F. Pessoa, Stefano Pigola, Alberto G. Setti

item.title: Rigidity of Immersed Gauss Curvature Shrinkers in Euclidean Space
item.description: arXiv:2610.14554v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every $m\geq2$, we prove that any connected closed oriented smooth immersion $X:M^m\to\mathbb{R}^{m+1}$ satisfying \[ K=\left\langle X,\nu\right\rangle \] is an embedding onto the unit sphere. No convexity is assumed. At a point maximizing $|X|$, we find a strictly convex component of $\{K>0\}$. If this component does not coincide with $M$, its polar immersion bounds an unbounded convex set. A finite area lemma then extends the local surface area formula for the polar body to a global measure identity. Using the vanishing first moment of surface area measure, we show that the origin lies in the interior of the polar body, contradicting the existence of recession directions. Thus the hypersurface is strictly convex, and the classification of strictly convex shrinkers completes the proof.
item.dc:creator: Jiahao Wang

item.title: Orbit stratifications and smooth topology of positively curved six-manifolds with rank-one nonabelian symmetry
item.description: arXiv:2610.14582v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study closed simply connected six-manifolds with positive sectional curvature and an effective isometric action of $SO(3)$ or $SU(2)$. Starting from Liu's corrected orbit-space analysis, we refine the stratification and recover smooth topology in several previously unresolved cases. For a boundaryless $SO(3)$ quotient, singular isotropy is connected, the weighted nonprincipal graph belongs to nine necessary families, and every action with only cyclic exceptional isotropy is classified equivariantly. The remaining branching families admit explicit rational intersection and Pontryagin formulas. For a three-ball $SO(3)$ quotient, the uniform-boundary configurations give sphere bundles over $S^4$ and a completely distinguished odd-integer family of non-spin six-manifolds. A doubled-quotient argument excludes the configuration with two boundary fixed points and an interior singular orbit, while the configuration with one fixed point and an exceptional interval has underlying manifold $\mathbb{CP}^3$. For a boundaryless $SU(2)$ quotient, an adjoint-weight matching argument reduces the exceptional three-orbit case to a unique action on the Eschenburg flag and identifies every two-orbit candidate with a weighted action on $S^2\times S^4$. These classifications imply rational ellipticity throughout the stated symmetry class. We also establish restricted curvature obstructions for the two diagonal product actions, without asserting nonexistence for arbitrary invariant metrics. Abstract graph restrictions, smooth realizability, and positive-curvature realizability are kept distinct. Some of the results in this paper are discovered by ChatGPT-6-astra and verified by the authors.
item.dc:creator: Minbo Gao, Yuhang Liu

item.title: $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$-cohomology on multidifferential operators space
item.description: arXiv:2610.14820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute cohomology spaces of the ortosymplectic Lie superalgebra $\mathfrak{osp}(1|2)$ on the (1,1)-dimensional real superspace with coefficients in the superspace $\frak{D}_{{\lambda},\mu}$ of $n$-ary differential operators acting on weighted densities (${\lambda}\in\mathbb{R}^n$ and $\mu\in\mathbb{R}$).
item.dc:creator: Mabrouk Ben Ammar, Amina Jabeur

item.title: Global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate for complex Monge--Amp\`ere equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.14870v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove a global $C^{2,\alpha}$ estimate for the complex Monge--Amp\`ere equation with a positive $C^\alpha$ right-hand side on a compact K\"ahler manifold.
item.dc:creator: Haozhao Li, Bing Wang, Kai Zheng

item.title: Anomaly Flow II: Estimates and Long-time Existence for the Coupled Flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.15009v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this follow-up to \cite{Sua25}, we extend the results to the coupled anomaly flow which incorporates the evolution of a Hermitian metric on a holomorphic vector bundle over a compact complex $3$-fold with general slope parameter $\alpha'$. This yields a similar sufficient smallness condition on the slope parameter $\alpha'$ in order to extend the flow on $[0, \tau)$ to $[0, \tau + \epsilon)$. We also augment the argument of \cite{Sua25} slightly to fix the peculiarity of the units in the condition for $\alpha'$ for the $k = 1$ case.
item.dc:creator: Caleb Suan

item.title: Strongly isotropy irreducible spaces whose Laplacians have all their eigenspaces irreducible
item.description: arXiv:2610.15113v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $H$ be a closed subgroup of a compact connected Lie group $G$ such that $G/H$ is simply connected, the action of $G$ on $G/H$ is almost effective, and $G/H$ is a strongly isotropy irreducible space. The smallest positive eigenvalue of the Laplace-Beltrami operator $\Delta$ associated to the standard metric on $G/H$ was recently computed. In this article we obtain a second non-zero eigenvalue of $\Delta$. As a consequence, we prove that all eigenspaces of the Laplacian are irreducible as $G$-modules if and only if $(G,H)$ is a compact symmetric pair of real rank one, or $(G,H)$ is equal to $(\operatorname{G}_2,\operatorname{SU}(3))$ or $(\operatorname{Spin}(7),\operatorname{G}_2)$.
item.dc:creator: Emilio A. Lauret, Fiorela Rossi Bertone

item.title: Holomorphic Bisectional Curvature on Total Spaces of Holomorphic Vector Bundles
item.description: arXiv:2610.15271v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study complete K$\"a$hler metrics with prescribed signs of holomorphic bisectional curvature on total spaces of holomorphic vector bundles over compact complex manifolds. We establish necessary and sufficient conditions in the nonnegative and strictly negative cases, characterized respectively by unitary flatness and Griffiths negativity of the bundle, together with the corresponding curvature conditions on the base. We also obtain a global metric splitting in the nonnegative case, rule out strictly positive curvature over positive-dimensional bases, and construct counterexamples to the converse in the nonpositive case.
item.dc:creator: Xingluan Wang

item.title: On the Structure of the Cut Locus in Certain Classes of Warped Product Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.15279v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we determine the structure of the cut locus for a class of complete warped product manifolds $M=(R^1\times S^1,dt^2+m(t)^2d\theta^2)$, where the warping function $m(t)$ is positive and even, under the assumption that there exists a positive number $t_1$ such that the Gaussian curvature is nonpositive on the domain $t^{-1}\left((t_1,\infty) \right)$ and is decreasing along the subarc $t^{-1}([0,t_1])\cap\theta^{-1}(0)$ of the upper half meridian.
item.dc:creator: Nathaphon Boonnam

item.title: Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for closed axisymmetric hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.15311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish sharp Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities for closed, embedded, axisymmetric hypersurfaces Sigma in n+1 dimensional Euclidean space R^{n+1}, the dimension n > or = 2, with admissible C^{1,1} profiles. Let H_j be the j-th normalized mean curvature. If Sigma is axiconvex, i.e., every hyperplane orthogonal to the symmetry axis meets the enclosed domain in an n-dimensional ball or empty, then \[\left(\frac{\int_\Sigma H_\ell\,dA}{|\mathbb S^n|}\right)^{1/(n-\ell)} \le \left(\frac{\int_\Sigma H_k\,dA}{|\mathbb S^n|}\right)^{1/(n-k)}, \qquad 0\le\ell<k\le n-1. \] Without axiconvexity, the inequalities hold for sign-corrected integrals \[\int_\Sigma\varepsilon_\theta^{\,j}H_j\,dA,\] where varepsilon_{theta}= {sgn}(sin {theta}) denotes the sign of the azimuthal principal curvatures. As applications, the Alexandrov--Fenchel inequalities remain valid whenever both l and k are even. Equality in each of the above inequalities holds if and only if Sigma is a round sphere. The proof adapts the rearrangement and tangent angle folding approach of Dalphin-Henrot-Masnou-Takahashi from surfaces of revolution in R^3 to n-dimensional axisymmetric hypersurfaces in R^{n+1}. The higher-dimensional construction uses weighted monotone rearrangement to produce convex comparison bodies with C^{1,1} boundaries.
item.dc:creator: Weimin Sheng, Yinhang Wang

item.title: A note on the Chern-Yamabe flow on compact Hermitian manifolds with negative Gauduchon degree
item.description: arXiv:2610.15326v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this note, we prove that on a compact Hermitian manifold with negative Gauduchon degree, the Chern-Yamabe flow introduced in our recent work [13] converges to the solution of prescribed Chern scalar curvature problem, provided that the candidate curvature function is nonpositive and not identically zero.
item.dc:creator: Weike Yu

item.title: Hypersurfaces with constant sectional curvature of a product of two space forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.15489v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We complete the classification of hypersurfaces with constant sectional curvature of dimension greater than or equal to three in the product of two space forms.
item.dc:creator: Jihun Kim, Yuri Nikolayevsky, Ruy Tojeiro

item.title: Remarks on the disjoint minimal graphs conjecture
item.description: arXiv:2610.15736v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is known that there can be at most 3 disjoint nontrivial minimal graphs in R^3 with 0 boundary values, and conjectured that there can be at most 2. We explore properties that the graphs would have if there were 3.
item.dc:creator: Allen Weitsman

item.title: Auxiliary Hessian Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15866v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose k-Hessian equations as auxiliary equations for degenera- tions of K\"ahler classes to nef classes of numerical dimension k. As proof-of-concept results, we provide a uniform mean-value inequality and uniform \`a priori estimates for Hessian equa- tions.
item.dc:creator: Johannes G. Scheffler

item.title: Stability of Diophantine Minimal Foliations in Arbitrary Codimension
item.description: arXiv:2610.15984v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We generalize Moser's stability theorem for minimal hypersurface foliations to arbitrary codimension. Let $\mathbb{T}^N=\mathbb{R}^N/\mathbb{Z}^N$ be the standard torus, and let $P\subset\mathbb{R}^N$ be an $m$-plane satisfying a Diophantine condition relative to $\mathbb{Z}^N$. We prove that, under every sufficiently small smooth $\mathbb{Z}^N$-periodic perturbation of the Euclidean metric, the affine foliation of $\mathbb{T}^N$ induced by $P$ persists as a smoothly conjugate foliation by minimal $m$-dimensional submanifolds. The normalized conjugating displacement depends smoothly and tamely on the metric and is locally unique. The proof uses Hamilton's formulation of the Nash-Moser implicit function theorem.
item.dc:creator: Hoan Nguyen

item.title: A Dimension Estimate for Polynomial Growth Holomorphic Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.16174v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: On a complete noncompact K\"ahler manifold $M^n$ of complex dimension $n$ with nonnegative Ricci curvature, we prove that polynomial growth holomorphic functions of degree $d$ ($d\geq 0$) have an dimension upper bound $C(n)(1+d)^n$. In particular, $\dim_{\C}\OO_d(M)\leq C'(n)d^n,$ for $d\geq1$, and the estimate is sharp.
item.dc:creator: Haohao Wang

item.title: Higher order isoperimetric inequalities and rigidity for surfaces in $\R^n$
item.description: arXiv:2610.16221v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a family of sharp higher order isoperimetric type inequalities for smooth compact surfaces in Euclidean spaces of arbitrary codimension. These inequalities involve arbitrarily high derivatives of the boundary curve, together with the mean curvature vector of the surface. For example, the first and second order inequalities yield the sharp two-sided estimate for the isoperimetric deficit: \begin{align*} & \frac{\pi}{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-R\nu|^2\, ds +2\pi\int_M x\cdot H\, dA \le L^2-4\pi A\\ \le& \frac{\pi}{R}\int_{\partial M}|x-R\nu|^2\, ds +2\pi\int_M x\cdot H\, dA +\frac{\pi}{3R}\int_{\partial M}|x+R^2\kappa|^2\, ds, \end{align*} where $R=\frac{L}{2\pi}$ and the origin is chosen to be the centroid of the boundary. For minimal surfaces, equality in the lower bound holds precisely for flat disks, whereas the second inequality admits non-round equality cases. Our results extend that of Carleman, Sachs, Chakerian, and Li-Schoen-Yau. A distinctive feature of our work is the unexpected rigidity structure arising at higher orders. At the first and second orders, equality curves admit decompositions into circular Fourier modes supported in mutually orthogonal planes. Remarkably, this phenomenon fails at higher orders. We establish a multiplicative factorization of the unit tangent map into elementary planar rotations acting on a fixed unit vector, providing a characterization of equality cases at arbitrary order. As a result, we construct a third order equality curve in $\mathbb R^3$ whose Fourier modes cannot be decomposed into mutually orthogonal circular modes.
item.dc:creator: Xu-Qian Fan, Kwok-Kun Kwong

item.title: Optimal Synthesis on the Special Linear Group
item.description: arXiv:2610.16222v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the exponential map on the group of real two-by-two matrices with determinant one, endowed with a left-invariant Riemannian metric. Using the Euler-Poincar\'e equation and its linearization, we determine the conjugate and Maxwell times and identify a domain on which the exponential map is a global diffeomorphism onto the complement of the Maxwell stratum. This provides an alternative proof that the first Maxwell time coincides with the cut time. We obtain an explicit matrix description of the cut locus and characterize the globally minimizing geodesics. Furthermore, we analyze the first Maxwell-time function, determine its unique global minimum, and show that the injectivity radius is $\frac{\pi \sqrt{14}}{4}$. Finally, we characterize the intersection of the cut and conjugate loci and prove that every geodesic is equi-optimal.
item.dc:creator: Marcus T. C. Lau, Alejandro Bravo-Doddoli

item.title: Four-dimensional almost-Einstein manifolds with circulant structures
item.description: arXiv:2610.16377v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper considers a four-dimensional Riemannian manifold with an additional circulant tensor structure $Q$. We prove that such a manifold is almost-Einstein if the curvature tensor preserves the action of the structure on the last two arguments. Additionally, we examine an associated Riemannian product manifold $(M, g, Q)$ where $P=Q^{2}$, deriving explicit expressions for the curvature tensor in terms of the metric and the product structure. The sectional and Ricci curvatures of these manifolds are determined using special bases generated by the images of a given vector under the structure $Q$. Finally, we construct a non-trivial example of a four-dimensional locally product manifold by embedding a four-dimensional hypersurface into a ten-dimensional Euclidean space.
item.dc:creator: Iva Dokuzova, Georgi Dzhelepov, Dimitar Razpopov

item.title: Biconservative hypersurfaces in Euclidean Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16434v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An isometric immersion $X: \Sigma^n \longrightarrow \mathbb{E}^{n+1}$ is biharmonic (BHH) if $\Delta^2 X = 0$, i.e., if $\Delta H =0$, where $\Delta$ and $H$ are the metric Laplacian and the mean curvature vector field of $\Sigma^n$ respectively. More generally, biconservative hypersurfaces (BCHs) are isometric immersions for which only the tangential part of the biharmonic equation vanishes. BCHs are first described and then constructed.
item.dc:creator: Hiba Bibi, Marc Soret, Marina Ville

item.title: On the Weyl tube formula for nonlocal perimeters
item.description: arXiv:2610.16461v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the asymptotic behaviour of the nonlocal perimeter of tubular neighbourhoods. For a closed $C^{1,1}$ submanifold of Euclidean space, we show that a suitable rescaling of the nonlocal perimeter of its tube converges to an explicit constant times the Hausdorff measure of the submanifold. The constant is the fractional perimeter of the unit ball in the codimension of the submanifold. For finite point sets, we obtain an exact tube formula in terms of a generalised hypergeometric function. In contrast with the classical Weyl formula, this expansion has infinitely many terms, contains both noninteger and integer powers of the tubular radius, and has coefficients that depend on the relative positions of the points rather than only on their intrinsic geometry. We also establish a point-set expansion for general analytic kernels.
item.dc:creator: Serena Dipierro, Jack Thompson, Enrico Valdinoci

item.title: The triangular metric on projective surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16487v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In \cite{ThurstonStretch} Thurston introduced stretch paths and stretch maps between hyperbolic surfaces. In this paper we extend similar constructions to the space of convex real projective structures on surfaces. Using Fock-Goncharov-like parameters, we introduce stretch paths and construct explicit stretch maps between the projective surface. We show that stretch maps are $e^t$--Lipschitz with respect to a triangular metric we introduce on the projective surface. This allows us to gain control on several length functions on an open set of the space of convex real projective structures (those where there is no ``local back--tracking"). As an application we obtain pointwise upper bounds for the Hilbert entropy of some convex real projective structures in terms of Fock-Goncharov-like parameters.
item.dc:creator: Le\'on Carvajales, Xian Dai, Beatrice Pozzetti, Anna Wienhard

item.title: Ricci pinching on complete Kahler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.16563v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study Ricci pinching problem on complete K\"ahler manifolds. For complete noncompact manifolds with Euclidean volume growth, we prove flatness under nonnegative bisectional curvature and Ricci pinching, and Ricci flatness under nonnegative Ricci curvature, quadratic curvature decay, and the same pinching condition. In both cases, the pinching constant may tend to zero at a logarithmic rate. Examples show that the logarithmic exponent is sharp in complex dimension two. Second part of the paper proves that a complete K\"ahler manifold of complex dimension at least two with positive holomorphic bisectional curvature is compact if its sectional curvature is nonnegative and its Ricci curvature is uniformly pinched outside a compact set. No volume-growth assumption or curvature upper bound is needed. Heat smoothing of the Busemann function supplies a strictly plurisubharmonic exhaustion with bounded gradient, so the general top Ricci-mass theorem of Datar--Pingali--Seshadri applies. The new ingridents are integral estimates for the Ricci form. The analytic arguments use scalar curvature gap theorems and a critical-$L^n$ vanishing theorem for closed real $(1,1)$-forms under nonnegative Ricci curvature and nonnegative quadratic orthogonal bisectional curvature. The Hodge-Laplace heat eqution deformation conserves the signed top-degree integral, including its initial value, while norm domination and scalar heat-semigroup decay force this integral to vanish. For semipositive initial forms this gives pointwise vanishing of the top wedge power.
item.dc:creator: Gang Liu, Lei Ni

item.title: Sharp parameter gaps for quantized Mabuchi energies and cscK metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.16697v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For polarized manifolds, we show that semistability for the quantized Mabuchi energy at one fixed finite parameter is equivalent to uniform K-stability and to unique existence of constant scalar curvature K\"ahler (cscK) metrics. We obtain sharp comparisons between quantized Mabuchi slopes at different parameters and with the ordinary Mabuchi slope. In the presence of automorphisms, we give an equivariant criterion using torus twists under the vanishing of the Futaki character. The estimates also hold for finite-energy geodesic rays in compact K\"ahler classes. On a fixed ruled surface with discrete automorphism group, we construct cscK polarizations with unbounded critical parameters. Their ratios to the $\alpha$-invariant are also unbounded.
item.dc:creator: Kefeng Liu, Liangdi Zhang

item.title: Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature in complex space forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.16767v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M$ be a connected Hamiltonian stationary Lagrangian surface of constant Gaussian curvature $K$ in a two-dimensional complex space form $\Mtilde^2(4\epsilon)$ of constant holomorphic sectional curvature $4\epsilon$, and let $H$ denote its mean curvature vector field. We prove that either $K=\epsilon$ or $K=0\ne\epsilon$ and $|H|$ is constant. In particular, if $|H|$ is non-constant, then $K=\epsilon$.
item.dc:creator: Toru Sasahara

item.title: Non-algebraicity of the Lawson surfaces $\xi_{k,l}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.16853v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every Lawson surface $\xi_{k,l}\subset\mathbb S^3$ of genus $kl>1$ is non-algebraic: any real polynomial vanishing on $\xi_{k,l}$ vanishes identically on $\mathbb S^3$. This answers a question posed by Hsiang in 1967 and proves Lawson's 1970 conjecture for $\xi_{2,2}$. The proof uses a reflection principle for the monodromy of the associated family of flat connections.
item.dc:creator: Lynn Heller, Sebastian Heller

item.title: Spectral and Nodal Properties of Static Manifolds with Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.16974v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study compact static manifolds with boundary from a spectral point of view, with particular emphasis on the relation between Dirichlet, Neumann, and Robin spectra and the nodal structure of static potentials. We establish comparison inequalities linking Dirichlet and Neumann eigenvalues with the scalar curvature and derive sufficient spectral conditions ensuring that a static potential changes sign. We also obtain bounds on the number of connected components of the zero set, sufficient conditions for its connectedness, and sufficient conditions ensuring that its components intersect the boundary. Finally, we study variational properties of Robin static triples and characterize compact Robin static triples whose metrics are critical for the first mixed Robin--Dirichlet eigenvalue under admissible volume-preserving deformations.
item.dc:creator: Vladimir Medvedev

item.title: The index of conformal Hopf maps
item.description: arXiv:2610.17087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We compute the index and nullity of any harmonic morphism from $S^3$ to $S^2$.
item.dc:creator: Eric Loubeau, Radu Slobodeanu

item.title: On the collapsing of spaces with local rewinding Reifenberg control
item.description: arXiv:2610.17229v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(M^n,g_0)$ be a complete Riemannian manifold with $\Ric_{g_0}\ge-(n-1)g_0$ whose local universal covers are uniformly $\delta$-Reifenberg-close to $\R^n$ below a fixed radius $\rho$. We show that for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$ there are $\delta(n,\alpha)>0$ and $T(n,\rho,\alpha)>0$ such that, if $\delta\le\delta(n,\alpha)$, a complete Ricci flow $g(t)$ with $g(0)=g_0$ and $|\Rm_{g(t)}|\le\alpha/t$ exists on $(0,T]$. On closed manifolds this is a uniform lower bound for the lifetime of the Ricci flow; on noncompact manifolds, where the initial curvature may be unbounded, it is an existence theorem, and the flow is unique among complete Ricci flows from $g_0$ with a curvature bound of the form $A/t$. The key step is a finite-buffer comparison of two Ricci flows through the Ricci--harmonic map heat flow, following Lee, which transfers a Type-I curvature bound from a complete selected flow to the incomplete flow lifted to a local cover. Consequently, below a dimensional Reifenberg threshold, collapsing closed manifolds admit singular nilpotent fibrations over their Gromov--Hausdorff limits. The Reifenberg hypothesis cannot be weakened to noncollapsing of the local covers: products of shrinking circles with Nifa's four-manifolds have $\Ric\ge0$ and uniformly noncollapsed local covers, but admit no continuous Gromov--Hausdorff approximations onto their limit.
item.dc:creator: Shaosai Huang

item.title: Compactness of Cone Yang-Mills Connections
item.description: arXiv:2610.17472v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the cone Yang-Mills functional recently introduced by Tseng and Zhou. This functional generalizes the Yang-Mills functional by coupling it to a closed 2-form which can represent a geometric structure of interest, e.g. a symplectic form or Ricci form. While the perspective of dimensional reduction is not always possible, we show that a cone Yang-Mills field is always locally the dimensional reduction of a pure Yang-Mills field. We then prove a monotonicity formula and use the dimensional reduction framework to prove an $\epsilon$-regularity theorem in two ways. Finally, we prove a compactness theorem for sequences of cone Yang-Mills connections with bounded action and $L^p$-bounded Higgs fields. Away from a singular set of codimension at least 4 and after suitable bundle identifications, the sequence subconverges in the $C^\infty_{\operatorname{loc}}$-topology.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Delgado

item.dc:creator: Jiayu Li, Lei Liu, Yanjun Liu, Mingyuan Zhu

item.title: Constant Rank Theorems under Intermediate Ricci Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.17691v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove two constant rank theorems for the Ricci tensor in two geometric settings: manifolds with harmonic curvature and gradient Ricci solitons. In both cases, if the $k$-intermediate Ricci curvature satisfies $\Ric_k\geq0$ for some $1\leq k\leq n-2$, then the Ricci tensor has constant rank and its nullity distribution is parallel. In the complete case, the universal cover splits isometrically along the Ricci-null directions. We also show that the range $1\leq k\leq n-2$ is sharp: in every dimension $n\geq4$, nonnegative Ricci curvature alone does not imply the constant rank property in either setting.
item.dc:creator: Mijia Lai, Guoqiang Wu

item.title: Existence and uniqueness of conformal Gauduchon metrics
item.description: arXiv:2610.17858v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove that every Hermitian conformal class on a connected noncompact complex manifold of dimension at least two contains a Gauduchon metric. We give a sufficient condition for uniqueness of such Gauduchon metrics up to scaling in terms of functions bounded from above and their Levi forms. This condition is necessary when the manifold has at least two ends. In that case, uniqueness in a fixed conformal class is equivalent to the assertion that every positive solution of the complex Laplace equation for a metric in that class is constant. For a connected noncompact complex Lie group of dimension $n$, uniqueness in every conformal class is equivalent to the assertion that, for every Hermitian metric, every positive solution of the complex Laplace equation is constant. These properties hold exactly when the complex tangent space of a maximal compact subgroup has dimension $n-1$; such a group is abelian. In a conformal class containing a balanced metric, the same equivalence holds without a restriction on the number of ends. We also prove uniqueness for manifolds with a suitable potential on a compactification with compact fibers over a point, the real line, or a parabolic Riemann surface. The examples include compact pluripolar deletions, partially deleted compact fibers, and semipositive line bundles. We construct conformal Gauduchon metrics which are not related by scaling on Stein manifolds and on the total space of $\mathcal O_{\PP^1}(1)^{\oplus2}$.
item.dc:creator: Hanzhang Yin

item.title: A stationary harmonic map with a nonstationary tangent map
item.description: arXiv:2610.17938v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct a stationary weakly harmonic map from a domain in \R^5 into a compact K\"ahler surface for which a tangent map is weakly harmonic but nonstationary. The target manifold is the blow-up of \CP^1\times\CP^1 at four points lying in one fiber and arranged at the vertices of a regular tetrahedron. The nonstationarity of the tangent map arises from the break down of the tetrahedral symmetry in the defect measure concentrated on the vertices.
item.dc:creator: Siran Li, Zijun Wang

item.title: Equivariant analytic torsion forms
item.description: arXiv:2610.17960v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we first construct infinitesimal equivariant analytic torsion forms for K\"ahler fibrations. We then compare them with Ma's equivariant analytic torsion forms, modulo $\partial$- and $\overline{\partial}$-exact forms, in terms of equivariant Bott--Chern currents and the $I$-genus. Our comparison formula extends that of Bismut and Goette to families.
item.dc:creator: Yuxiang Li

item.title: Tournaments, flags, and spinors
item.description: arXiv:2610.18084v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is observed that the dimension of the space of invariant spinors on the manifold $\mathrm{SU}(n)/T^{n-1}$ of full flags in $\mathbb{C}^n$ equals the number $\mathrm{RT}(n)$ of labelled regular tournaments of order $n$, for $n$ odd. This space is decomposed under a double cover of the Weyl group, and realized as a pair of eigenspaces, first for the Dirac operator, then for a twisted version of it which acts equivariantly; this is used to show that multiplicities of irreducible representations are even for $n\equiv 1\pmod 4$.
item.dc:creator: Diego Conti, Simon Salamon

item.title: Singularities of Mean Curvature Flow with Bounded Total Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.18197v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove that every tangent flow at the first singular time of a smooth, closed, embedded mean curvature flow has smooth support, provided that the total curvature satisfies $\sup_{t\in[0,T)}\int_{M_t}|A|^n\,d\mu_t<\infty$. This extends Ilmanen's smoothness result for tangent flows to higher dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Yongheng Han, Zhen Wang

item.title: T^2-invariant Einstein metrics on closed 4-manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.18219v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics with positive Ricci curvature on #_m(S^2 x S^2) for every integer $m>1$. These provide infinite family of Einstein metrics on closed $4$-manifolds with $\lambda>0$, which are in addition not Hermitian. We further establish the uniqueness of the $T^2$-invariant Einstein metrics on $S^4$, CP^2, S^2 x S^2, and CP^2#\bar{CP}^2.
item.dc:creator: Kyle Broder, Ramiro A. Lafuente

item.title: A topological sphere theorem for pinched Legendrian submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.18293v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $M^n$ be a closed simply connected Legendrian submanifold of $\mathbb S^{2n+1}$, where $n\geq5$, and let $\mathbf{B}$ and $\mathbf{H}=\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{B}$ denote its second fundamental form and mean-curvature vector. We prove that $M$ is homeomorphic to $\mathbb S^n$ if \begin{equation*} |\mathbf{B}|^2\leq \frac{(n-1)(n+2)}n+\frac{n^2+3n-2}{2n^2}|\mathbf{H}|^2-\frac{(n-1)(n-2)}{2n^2}|\mathbf{H}|\sqrt{|\mathbf{H}|^2+4n}. \end{equation*} The equality can be attained by the Calabi products, so simple connectivity cannot be omitted. For $n\geq4$, we also prove a sphere theorem under an explicit bound and the weaker assumption $b_1(M;\mathbb R)=0$. The proof combines phase-rotated Lawson--Simons variations with a systolic inequality for finite two-complexes. We also give local constructions showing that the pinching condition allows negative isotropic curvature at a point.
item.dc:creator: Qing Cui, Linlin Sun

item.title: Pseudolocality and strong uniqueness for complete Ricci flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.18364v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we prove a uniform pseudolocality theorem for smooth complete Ricci flows whose initial metrics have Ricci curvature bounded below and uniformly positive injectivity radius. No a priori curvature bound is assumed on the flow. As a consequence, we obtain strong uniqueness for smooth complete Ricci flows from a complete metric with the above geometric bounds. We also prove that every smooth complete Ricci flow from a complete Ricci-flat metric with uniformly positive injectivity radius is stationary. The same conclusion holds for any complete flat initial metric. In particular, we give an affirmative answer to Chen's question on the strong uniqueness of Ricci flow from Euclidean space in every dimension.
item.dc:creator: Shaochuang Huang, Zhuo Peng

item.title: Scalar curvature rigidity of small spherical caps with arbitrary fill-ins
item.description: arXiv:2610.18413v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove an analogue of Min-Oo's conjecture for sufficiently small spherical caps in the unit round sphere. For every dimension $n\ge3$, there exists $r_*(n)>0$ such that the following holds for every round cap of radius $0<r\le r_*(n)$: any smooth compact connected oriented Riemannian fill-in with the same intrinsic boundary metric and with scalar curvature and outward boundary mean curvature at least those of the cap is isometric to the cap.
item.dc:creator: Yiyue Zhang, Bowen Zhao

item.title: Curvature measures and volume preserving flows in h-convex geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.18423v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper, we introduce a concept of modified curvature measures for h-convex domains in hyperbolic space and prove a shifted version of the generalized Alexandrov theorem, which characterizes geodesic balls in hyperbolic space via modified curvature measures. This result generalizes the classical work of Kohlmann (1998). We further investigate a volume-preserving shifted $\alpha$-Gauss curvature flow for strictly h-convex hypersurfaces in hyperbolic space and prove that for any $\alpha>0$ the solution exists for all time and converges smoothly to a geodesic sphere. The theory of modified curvature measures developed in the first part serves as a key ingredient in characterizing the Hausdorff limit shape of the flow.
item.dc:creator: Xinxiu Zhang

item.title: Counterexamples to prescribed scalar curvature in the null case
item.description: arXiv:2610.18432v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We construct smooth functions on the flat torus $\mathbb{T}^{n\ge5}$ that change sign and have negative mean but cannot be realized as the scalar curvature of any metric in the given conformal class.
item.dc:creator: Yuxiang Li, Yunqing Wu, Jie Zhou

item.title: Curvature, diameter and bounded Betti numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.18530v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the image of the comparison homomorphism from bounded cohomology to ordinary cohomology. Its dimension is called the bounded Betti number. In our earlier work we proved that the total bounded Betti number of a closed Riemannian $n$-manifold satisfying $\Ric\geq -(n-1)$ and $\Diam\leq D$ is bounded by a constant depending only on $n$ and $D$. The original proof used the amenability of the images of sufficiently small local fundamental groups. Since that work was written, Kapovitch and Wilking proved Gromov's generalized Margulis lemma under a lower Ricci curvature bound. Their theorem gives the stronger conclusion that these local groups are uniformly virtually nilpotent. We explain how their result supplies a direct modern input for the bounded Betti number theorem. We also discuss the topological meaning of the bounded part of ordinary cohomology and its relation to the $\ell^1$-seminorm on homology.
item.dc:creator: Zhongmin Shen, Jyh-Yang Wu

item.title: A sharp pinching theorem for closed minimal Legendrian submanifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.18536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $F:M^n\to\mathbb{S}^{2n+1}$ be a minimal Legendrian immersion of a connected closed manifold, where $n\ge3$, and let $B$ be its second fundamental form. We prove that if $|B|^2\le(n-1)(n+2)/n$, then, up to a unitary transformation, $F$ parametrizes a totally geodesic sphere or is a finite covering of the image of the minimal Calabi product of a point and a totally geodesic Legendrian sphere. This proves Conjecture 1 of Luo and Sun [Ann. Inst. H. Poincar\'e C Anal. Non Lin\'eaire 40 (2023), p. 548].
item.dc:creator: Yong Luo, Linlin Sun, Jiabin Yin

item.title: The anisotropic Weyl law and Grassmannian equidistribution
item.description: arXiv:2610.18599v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We establish a Weyl law for the codimension-one anisotropic volume spectrum on compact Riemannian manifolds. We then use this law to obtain equidistribution in the full Grassmannian bundle while keeping the ambient metric fixed. More precisely, on every closed connected smooth Riemannian manifold of dimension three through six, we construct smooth, embedded hypersurfaces stationary for anisotropies smoothly converging to area. The cumulative sum of their area measures, when lifted to the Grassmannian bundle, converges to the uniform measure.
item.dc:creator: Antonio De Rosa, Aria Halavati

item.title: Odd-dimensional lens-space Yamabe counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2610.18662v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $n\ge5$ be odd and let \(L_{3q}^n=S^n/C_{3q}\) be the standard lens space, where $q>3$ is prime. We prove that for all sufficiently large $q$, \[ \sigma(L_{3q}^n) > (3q)^{-2/n}Y(S^n)=Y(L_{3q}^n,[g_{\rm rd}]). \] Here \([g_{\rm rd}]\) denotes the quotient-round conformal class. Combining spin bordism with the surgery theorem of Ammann--Dahl--Humbert, we establish \[ \sigma(L_{3q}^n)\ge \min \{q^{-2/n}Y(S^n),\Lambda_n\}, \] where $\Lambda_n>0$ depends only on $n$. For sufficiently large $q$, this exceeds the quotient-round value, showing that the quotient-round conformal class need not maximize the smooth Yamabe invariant in any odd dimension $n\ge5$.
item.dc:creator: Jakob Loren

item.title: Smooth approximation, Alexandrov-Fenchel type inequalities and curvature flows for h-convex bodies in hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2610.18761v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We associate each h-convex body in hyperbolic space $\mathbb{H}^{n+1}(n\geq 2)$ with a Radon measure valued $(0,2)$-tensor on the sphere $\mathbb{S}^n$ through its horospherical function. Using spherical convolution, we prove that any h-convex body can be approximated by a sequence of smooth strictly h-convex bodies in the Hausdorff sense. This approximation result extends the inequality parts of the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality to general h-convex bodies, but equality rigidity cannot be obtained directly. We prove that the equality holds in the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality and the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality if and only if the h-convex bodies are geodesic balls. For the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we establish the Hausdorff stability independent of curvature bounds described by the Alexandrov-Fenchel deficits for h-convex bodies, which implies the equality rigidity of the Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality. For the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality, we introduce a class of globally constrained $k$-th modified quermassintegrals preserving flows with general h-convex initial hypersurfaces to obtain the equality rigidity. Moreover, we prove the flows above preserve h-convexity, make the $(k+1)$-th modified quermassintegrals non-increasing and converge to geodesic spheres. We prove a rigidity theorem for modified area measures for h-convex bodies and use this rigidity theorem to characterize the geodesic balls via modified support measures for h-convex bodies, from which we prove that the $(k+1)$-th modified quermassintegrals strictly decrease in a short time along the flows with non-spherical initial hypersurfaces. Then we obtain the equality rigidity of the modified Alexandrov-Fenchel inequality.
item.dc:creator: Xinxiu Zhang

item.title: A three-block higher-rank deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills correspondence on $\mathbb P^1\times\mathbb P^1$
item.description: arXiv:2610.18788v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the invariant rank-four deformed Hermitian--Yang--Mills equation associated with the chain $\mathcal{O}(1)\to\mathcal{O}(2)^{\oplus2}\to\mathcal{O}(3)$ over $\mathbb P^1$, with vertical weights $(4,2,0)$ and a fixed product K\"ahler class and phase. For arbitrary linear arrows $\psi=Bz$ and $\phi=(Az)^T$, smooth strictly calibrated reduced solutions exist exactly when $A$ is invertible and $z^TA^TBz$ is not identically zero. The same condition characterizes stability, semistability and polystability in the specified equivariant coherent category. The classification includes all eleven nonempty coefficient strata and both coincident and distinct divisor points on the rank-one lower boundary. The analytic proof retains the ordered, noncommuting middle equation. After constructing positive-parameter solutions, it rules out unbounded metric values by combining the source budgets with moving spectral tests; on the rank-one lower boundary, the divisor mass must also be retained. Global value, gradient and symbol estimates then give a smooth strictly calibrated endpoint on the original chain. No equivalence with full coherent or derived-category stability, uniqueness, or estimate uniform across changing chains is asserted.
item.dc:creator: Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun

item.title: Sharp Yamabe Bounds for Spherical Three-Space Forms via Four-Dimensional Poincar\'e--Einstein Compactness
item.description: arXiv:2610.18793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Gamma<SO(4)$ be a nontrivial finite group acting freely on $S^3$, and let $M=S^3/\Gamma$. We prove that every smooth conformal class $C$ on $M$ satisfies \[ Y(M,C)\le |\Gamma|^{-2/3}Y(S^3), \] with equality for the quotient-round conformal class. Consequently, \[ \sigma(M)=|\Gamma|^{-2/3}Y(S^3). \] Our approach uses four-dimensional Poincar\'e--Einstein fillings of the ball. We first establish compactness for fillings whose conformal infinities range over a compact family of positive-scalar-curvature metrics. Since compactness alone does not guarantee continuation through degenerate Einstein metrics, we use equivariant Fredholm parity to obtain a filling with the prescribed boundary conformal class and group action. A common interior fixed point then makes the Li--Qing--Shi boundary test function invariant, and its descent to $M$ gives the sharp covering factor.
item.dc:creator: Jakob Loren

item.title: Exterior free-boundary minimal surfaces of every topological type with at least two ends
item.description: arXiv:2610.18832v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: An exterior free-boundary minimal surface is a properly immersed minimal surface in the complement of the open unit ball of $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose boundary lies on the unit sphere and meets it orthogonally. We prove that for all integers $\ell\geq2$, $b\geq1$ and $\gamma\geq0$ there is a connected, orientable, properly embedded exterior free-boundary minimal surface with $\ell$ ends, $b$ boundary components and genus $\gamma$. Its total curvature is finite, and its ends are parallel catenoidal ends of multiplicity one. By the theorem of Mazet and Mendes, a surface of this kind with one end is a rotational annulus. Hence the topological types of such embedded surfaces are exactly the annulus with one end and all types with at least two ends. There are two gluing constructions. For $\ell\geq3$ we stack $\ell$ sheets over a stable catenoidal annulus that meets the sphere along a circle of radius $4/5$, and we join adjacent sheets by half-catenoidal bridges sitting on the sphere. The sheets are small normal graphs over this annulus whose displacements contain different multiples of the Jacobi field of the family of such annuli, so their boundary circles and the logarithmic growth of their ends differ slightly. For $\ell=2$ we double a catenoidal annulus near the critical angle $\pi/4$, where it acquires a bounded rotationally invariant Jacobi field; the distance to the critical annulus is coupled to the size of the bridges. In gluing constructions inside the unit ball that double or stack a compact surface, the bridges themselves must balance the sheets, which forces many bridges. Here the logarithmic growth of the ends absorbs this balancing. A fixed number of bridges therefore suffices, and every topological type is reached, including the small ones.
item.dc:creator: Igor Kozyrev

item.title: On the Reverse Projection Inequality
item.description: arXiv:2610.13953v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In \cite {ChenFengLiXiXu2026}, a reverse projection inequality for general convex bodies was established in three dimensions. In this paper, we completely characterize the equality cases of this inequality. We further show that the reverse projection inequality fails in every dimension $n\geq9$. The counterexamples are constructed as full-dimensional polytopes with at most $n+2$ facets.
item.dc:creator: Yibin Feng, Shengnan Hu, Weiru Liu, Lei Xu

item.title: Polygons and coplanar points on submanifolds of codimension 2
item.description: arXiv:2610.14032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Problem 73 on Green's list of open problems asks whether a smooth submanifold of codimension two in $\mathbb{R}^n$ must meet some affine two-plane in five points when $n$ is large. In this paper, we answer this question for every $n \geq 6$. Every nonempty relatively open subset of such a submanifold contains the vertices of an affinely regular pentagon, and the bound $n \geq 6$ is sharp for affinely regular pentagons. More generally, for every prime $p \geq 5$, the graph of a continuous map from a ball in $\mathbb{R}^{p-1}$ to $\mathbb{R}^2$ contains an affinely regular $p$-gon. A second argument gives six coplanar points when $n \geq 7$. Both proofs find the points by making the low Fourier modes of the graph map vanish along a circle.
item.dc:creator: Sohail (Neel), Sarkar

item.title: Example of exponential many collisions of identical hard disks in the plane
item.description: arXiv:2610.14282v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,d) $ denote the maximal number of nonsimultaneous elastic collisions among $n$ identical hard balls moving freely in $\mathbb{R}^d$. We give a planar construction with exponential lower bound with respect to $n$: $ \operatorname{MaxCol}(n,2)\geq 2^{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}, \quad n\geq3 $.
item.dc:creator: Hongda Qiu

item.title: Yang-Mills Theory in the Multisymplectic Framework
item.description: arXiv:2610.14418v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This Master's thesis develops and applies the multisymplectic field-theory framework to (pure) Yang-Mills theory. Building from the geometric foundations of jet bundles and the Poincar\'e-Cartan forms, the work constructs the Lagrangian multisymplectic formalism for first-order field theories, recovering the usual Euler-Lagrange field equations and extending the Poisson brackets of symplectic mechanics to a full graded Lie algebra. It then establishes the Legendre correspondence with the multisymplectic Hamiltonian formalism (in which Hamilton equations are retrieved) including the case of singular Lagrangians (where a constraint algorithm is reproduced). Breaking Lorentz covariance via a Cauchy surface slicing, the thesis then relates the covariant multisymplectic picture to an instantaneous presymplectic (infinite-dimensional) formulation in which the instantaneous De Donder equations and presymplectic brackets are obtained in a compatible way. A comprehensive treatment of symmetries then leads to multisymplectic and instantaneous momentum maps generalizations and to several versions of Noether's theorems. Specializing the formalism to principal-bundle gauge theory, the thesis identifies the multisymplectic configuration space with the bundle of connections, gauge symmetries with symmetries in the multisymplectic language and builds the Yang-Mills Lagrangian. Lastly, among many computations, the standard tensorial Yang-Mills equations and the Bianchi identity in local trivializations are retrieved, Yang-Mills conserved currents and charges are obtained and the graded algebra is derived for a special class of Hamiltonian forms.
item.dc:creator: David Villa-Blanco

item.title: Localization of Floer homology for $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.14468v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith. The main construction is a stabilized chain complex. At every invariant intersection point we adjoin the Morse complex of a finite-dimensional normal spectral sphere, whose generators lie in free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbits. The differential counts holomorphic strips coupled to sphere half-trajectories by a one-sided weighted asymptotic evaluation. We prove transversality, a uniform spectral cutoff, and the compactification and gluing statements needed for the chain identity. The stabilized complex is quasi-isomorphic to the ordinary Floer complex and contains the complex of the fixed data as a subcomplex with free quotient, so the algebraic Smith inequality applies.
item.dc:creator: Erkao Bao, Tyler Lawson, Cheuk Yu Mak

item.title: Exponential Green energies, quantization, and minimizers on compact Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.15004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the exponential Green energies associated with a finite point configuration on a Riemann surface. We focus on studying optimal or close-to-optimal configurations, and show that they must be well-spread out on the surface. We study in particular the round sphere and obtain values for the minimal Green energy of a configuration. The first version of this paper was written with the help of ChatGPT.
item.dc:creator: Haakan Hedenmalm, Song-Yan Xie

item.title: A Half-Space Theorem for the Allen--Cahn Equation in All Dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2610.15014v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, in every dimension, a bounded, non-constant entire solution of the Allen--Cahn equation whose zero set is contained in a half-space is a one-dimensional heteroclinic solution.
item.dc:creator: Sanghoon Lee

item.title: Spectral G\aa rding Elliptic Equations
item.description: arXiv:2610.15434v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study spectral G\aa rding elliptic equations on compact K\"ahler manifolds. Smooth solvability is equivalent to the existence of a smooth representative in the admissible domain. The concavity theorem for ideal G\aa rding polynomials gives a fixed concave formulation to which Sz\'ekelyhidi's second-order argument applies in every degree $2\le d\le n$, extending Lin's top-degree solvability theorem. Combined with the numerical criteria of Fu--Li--Zhang--Zhang and Chen--Nie--Xu, this yields a Nakai--Moishezon type criterion for solvability on compact K\"ahler manifolds. A solution converts the local ideal G\aa rding structure into a global Lorentzian structure. Its mixed derivatives give a strict nonlinear Hodge--Riemann hierarchy from the degree of the equation down to degree two, and the homogenization of the intersection polynomial is Lorentzian in nef class directions. Numerical criteria then produce explicit Hodge--Riemann classes, Lefschetz isomorphisms in bidegree $(1,1)$, and weighted Hodge-index inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Hao Fang, Biao Ma

item.title: The Brakke-BV structure of flat flows
item.description: arXiv:2610.15511v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that, in ambient dimension at most seven, varifold limits of the minimizing movements scheme introduced by Almgren--Taylor--Wang and Luckhaus--Sturzenhecker are integral Brakke flows. As a consequence, we show that $L^1$-limit points of the scheme, usually known as flat flows, are generalized BV flows. The result is unconditional and, in particular, remains valid even in the absence of energy convergence and in the presence of fattening.
item.dc:creator: Daniele De Gennaro, Salvatore Stuvard

item.title: Sharp stability for mixed bubbles on hyperbolic space
item.description: arXiv:2610.15920v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove sharp residual stability estimates for the critical Poincar\'e-Sobolev equation near sums of one positive hyperbolic solution and one projected Euclidean bubble in dimensions at least four. The estimates are uniform in the relative positions of the centers. The sharp rate is linear except in dimension six, where it contains a square root of a logarithm. For nonnegative functions, the same estimates hold under an energy constraint near the sum of the two profile energies for \(\lambda\) outside a finite set, and an additional mass constraint removes this restriction. For arbitrary finite numbers of profiles, we identify and realize all nonnegative Palais-Smale levels. We characterize the parameters at which different pairs of profile numbers have the same energy and show that the limiting energy and mass determine both profile numbers.
item.dc:creator: Juncheng Wei, Zetian Yan, Zhipeng Yang

item.title: Regularity theorems for Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system
item.description: arXiv:2610.15952v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove several regularity theorems concerning Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the minimal surface system. The main lemma (i.e. ``Decoupling Lemma") says that the component functions of such solutions satisfy the homogeneous Pucci inequalities. This allows us to apply the regularity theory for scalar viscosity solutions for elliptic PDE component-wise to a viscosity solution for the system. As a result of the Decoupling Lemma, we deduce that 2D Lipschitz viscosity solutions to the system are analytic in the interior, and obtain a quantitative partial regularity theorem. We also prove a geometric Harnack inequality for Lipschitz solutions. The Harnack inequality yields a strong maximum principle and half-space Liouville theorem. Another significant consequence of the lemma is a boundary regularity theorem for Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Notably, our theorem does not require any density assumption at the graph boundary, and we do not assume stationarity. This is used to prove a classification theorem for the singular set of a 4D stationary solution on a bounded domain. We also prove an $\varepsilon$-regularity theorem extending a result of the author. To conclude, we survey open problems. As an example, we have included a Bernstein-type theorem for 3D homogeneous entire Lipschitz viscosity solutions. Taken together, our results suggest that viscosity methods are a useful tool for studying the regularity of minimal graphs.
item.dc:creator: Bryan Dimler

item.title: A Sharp Lower Bound for Integral Menger Curvature
item.description: arXiv:2610.15981v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that round circles $C_L$ are the unique minimisers of integral Menger curvature among embedded closed $C^1$ curves $\gamma$ of prescribed length $L$ for every $p\geq 2$, i.e. $M_p(C_L) \leq M_p(\gamma)$, with equality if and only if $\gamma$ parametrises a round circle. The proof combines a three-point symmetrisation, an analysis of diagonal truncations, and the periodic Wirtinger inequality. For $p>3$, known self-avoidance and regularity results extend the minimisation result to closed rectifiable curves without assuming embeddedness or smoothness, provided the length of the curve image equals $L$. In particular, $M_p$ detects the unknot and is basic for $p>3$, thereby answering a question posed repeatedly in the literature.
item.dc:creator: Sebastian Scholtes

item.title: Cubic moments of eigenfunctions on surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16157v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We identify Gaussian curvature as a local mechanism for cubic cancellation of Laplace eigenfunctions on Riemannian surfaces, without arithmetic or dynamical assumptions. For $L^2$-normalized local solutions at frequency $\lambda$, cubic integrals against smooth compactly supported weights tend to zero whenever the curvature is nonzero almost everywhere where the weight is nonzero. Finite-order nondegeneracy yields sharp polynomial decay rates. In particular, on closed surfaces with nowhere-vanishing curvature, we obtain the rate $O(\lambda^{-1/6})$, attained by spherical harmonics on the round sphere. This proves the cubic case of the Gaussian moment conjecture for all normalized real eigenfunctions on closed negatively curved surfaces. The local proof rests on an exact identity relating the reduced phase at a Fermat point to Gaussian curvature. On complete hyperbolic surfaces with positive systole, we also prove global $O((\log\lambda)^{-3/2})$ decay for $L^2$-normalized eigenfunctions and smooth weights with bounded covariant derivatives through order two, without assuming finite area.
item.dc:creator: Xing Wang, Cheng Zhang

item.title: Minimal time for heat observability on almost-Riemannian surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16568v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We determine the minimal observation time for the heat equation on a closed almost-Riemannian surface, for a class of observation sets leaving sufficiently thin collars around simple Baouendi-Grushin circles. The structure and density are analytic near these circles, and the coefficients may depend on both variables. The formula is expressed through a complex phase describing concentration near the singular set and extends the thresholds known for separated models. Regular unobserved regions away from the circles do not change this time, provided all other singularities are observed. For singular circles of constant bracket step greater than two, local analyticity implies failure of observability at every time for observation sets at positive distance. We also construct quasimodes concentrated near simple singular circles, with exponentially small errors. Their superpositions give a lower bound for the Schr\"odinger observation time.
item.dc:creator: Vincent Boulard, Amaury Hayat, Emmanuel Tr\'elat

item.title: On the singular set of the geodesic flow on nonpositively curved surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.16612v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that the singular locus of the geodesic flow on the unit tangent bundle of a nonpositively curved surface enjoys an additional regularity property: its characteristic function belongs to the geometric anisotropic Sobolev space $H^{5/8-}_xH^{-13/16}_\theta$. In particular, this implies that if the geodesic flow is not ergodic with respect to the Liouville measure, then the zero set of the curvature must be thick in the sense that it supports a nonzero, nonnegative function in $H^{5/8-}$. The proof relies on semiclassical analysis and a new radial estimate for parabolic flows.
item.dc:creator: Thibault Lefeuvre

item.title: Regularity theory for lattice based harmonic maps and low temperature Gibbs measures of the spin-$O(N)$ model
item.description: arXiv:2610.16833v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The purpose of this note is twofold. First, we revisit the classical regularity theory of harmonic maps in the setting of maps defined on a lattice $\mathbb{Z}^d$ instead of $\mathbb{R}^d$ or some other manifold. The target space of our harmonic maps will be spheres $\mathbb{S}^{N-1}, N\geq 2$. A harmonic map $\sigma : \mathbb{Z}^d \to \mathbb{S}^{N-1}$ is a map which in any finite subgraph $\Lambda$ minimizes the internal Dirichlet energy $\frac 1 2 \sum_{i \sim j \in \Lambda} \|\sigma_i -\sigma_j\|^2$ given the boundary condition $\sigma_{|\partial \Lambda}$. One key difference between our setting and the continuum is that our main H\"older regularity statement in a large domain $\Lambda\subset \mathbb{Z}^{d=2}$ does not require any regularity assumption on the map $\sigma$ restricted to the boundary of the domain. For example, when $d=2$ and $N=3$, the H\"older regularity induced in the bulk of the domain holds uniformly in all boundary configurations $\sigma \in (\mathbb{S}^{2})^{\partial \Lambda}$ (this is in contrast with the continuum which requires extensions in suitable Sobolev spaces). The fact we obtain results uniformly in the boundary conditions allows us to extend our results for positive temperatures. Namely, as $T \searrow 0$, we obtain a local regularity theory for all infinite volume Spin $O(N)$ Gibbs measures, at least when $d=2$ and $N\geq 3$. We also discuss implications of our analysis in dimensions $d\geq 3$.
item.dc:creator: Christophe Garban, Nathan de Montgolfier

item.title: The Adiabatic b-Calculus and the Global Anomaly Formula on Manifolds with Boundary
item.description: arXiv:2610.16938v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the determinant line bundle for a family of elliptic operators on compact manifolds with boundary with the associated Quillen metric and Bismut-Freed connection, and we prove the global anomaly formula in this context. This extends Witten's holonomy theorem to manifolds with boundary. Witten studied the limiting behavior of the eta invariant of a Dirac operator on the total space of a fibration over $\mathbb{S}^1$ when the metric in the base $\mathbb{S}^1$ is blown up in a certain manner, a process known as taking the adiabatic limit. In this paper, we construct the calculus of adiabatic $b$-pseudodifferential operators, which naturally synthesizes the $b$-calculus and the adiabatic calculus of pseudodifferential operators. Using this calculus, and assuming the fiber operators to be invertible, we compute the adiabatic limit of the natural eta invariant in this setting and relate it to the integral of the Bismut-Freed connection and new correction terms coming from the boundary of the fibers.
item.dc:creator: Chad Nelson

item.title: Intrinsic Geometry Matching: learning observation-equivariant process geometry
item.description: arXiv:2610.16995v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Real data are often arbitrary, indirect observations of an unknown underlying process, and those observations can distort its geometry. Existing geometric methods equip data with the induced geometry of the ambient space, but this entangles the true geometry of the process with the distortion of the observation. To address this, we introduce Intrinsic Geometry Matching (IGM): a scalable approach to learn the intrinsic geometry of the underlying process. Specifically, we learn the carr\'e du champ operator of the process, allowing us to recover its diffusion geometry. Our method uses the fact that data often come with natural perturbations, like steps in a time series, to recover the intrinsic carr\'e du champ while transforming naturally with changes in observation: it is observation-equivariant. Furthermore, since this equivariance relates the geometry of different spaces, we can train a model using additional sources of data, even when that data lies in another space. We evaluate IGM on molecular dynamics, image, and video data and find better performance and scaling than existing neural and graph-based geometric tools.
item.dc:creator: Manuel Lecha, Michael Bronstein, Iolo Jones

item.title: Intrinsic Rigidity of Bar-and-Joint Frameworks on Riemannian Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.17004v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We develop an intrinsic rigidity theory for bar-and-joint frameworks whose vertices are constrained to a Riemannian manifold and whose edges are given by minimizing geodesic arcs. Such frameworks are called rigid if they cannot be deformed beyond the ambient isometries, while preserving the geodesic edge lengths. For admissible placements, for which adjacent vertices are joined by unique minimizing geodesics, we define a coordinate-free rigidity operator as the differential of the squared geodesic distance of the edges. By the first-variation formula, its edge rows are expressed in terms of the Riemannian logarithm, providing an intrinsic analogue of the classical Euclidean rigidity matrix. Trivial motions are characterized by orbits of the diagonal action of the isometry group, leading to notions of infinitesimal and local rigidity. We further develop a covariant second-order rigidity theory using the Riemannian Hessians of the edge constraints and characterize second-order rigidity through self-stresses and associated quadratic forms. Finally, we show that infinitesimal and second-order rigidity can be used as sufficient conditions for the local rigidity of an intrinsic framework. Our overarching goal is to provide a unified differential-geometric formulation of intrinsic framework rigidity on smooth manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Matthias Adrian-Himmelmann

item.title: Identifiability and Consistent Recovery for the Unnormalized Graph Laplace Operators
item.description: arXiv:2610.17032v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study whether an unnormalized graph Laplace operator can determine both the geometry of a manifold and its sampling density. On a fixed compact smooth manifold without boundary, we use a known positive, continuous, strictly decreasing radial kernel at a fixed positive bandwidth. For positive sampling densities, the operator built from geodesic distances determines the Riemannian metric and identifies the density up to equality almost everywhere. When the metric is induced by a Euclidean embedding, the operator built from ambient distances also determines the embedding up to rotations, reflections and translations, and the density. On compact parameter classes with positive continuous densities, minimizing the distance between empirical and popula- tion operators gives estimates that converge to the true parameters under independent, identically distributed sampling. This recovery result assumes that the empirical operator can be evaluated at arbitrary points of the manifold.
item.dc:creator: Susovan Pal

item.title: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on symmetric spaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17045v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations are random tessellations that arise as limits of Voronoi diagrams for Poisson point processes as their intensity tends to zero. For the Riemannian metric on a symmetric space of higher rank, Fr\k{a}czyk, Mellick, and Wilkens (arXiv:2307.01194) proved that the corresponding ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellation is almost surely completely connected, with an unbounded side between any two cells. This contrasts sharply with the geometry of ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations in hyperbolic spaces studied by D'Achille, Curien, Enriquez, Lyons, and \"Unel (arXiv:2303.16831). In this paper we introduce and study ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations for Finsler metrics on higher rank symmetric spaces. We show that ideal Poisson--Voronoi tessellations with respect to polyhedral Finsler metrics can exhibit either behavior seen in these previous works: generically they resemble the hyperbolic case, where almost surely all cells have bounded sides. We further introduce the ideal Selberg--Poisson--Voronoi tessellation of the space of positive definite symmetric matrices, which has particularly nice properties.
item.dc:creator: Colin Davalo, J. Maxwell Riestenberg, Anna Wienhard

item.title: Finiteness of Fuchsian equations with unitarizable monodromy on compact Riemann surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.17116v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove that, on any compact Riemann surface, there are only finitely many meromorphic projective connections with prescribed singular points and real exponent differences whose projective monodromy is unitarizable. We also establish properness and growth estimates for holonomy, including a relative version for smooth marked families, and derive finiteness results for spherical conical metrics and ramification divisors of stable extensions.
item.dc:creator: Sheng Tan

item.title: Metaplectic-c prequantizations and the Einstein--Brillouin--Keller quantizability condition
item.description: arXiv:2610.17890v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We show that every symplectic manifold admits a symplectic form whose metaplectic-c prequantizations give quantizability conditions on all its Lagrangian submanifolds. Metaplectic-c prequantizations descend to prequantizations over the Lagrangian Grassmannian bundle that are fibrewise flat with holonomies primitive fourth roots of unity on the generators of the fundamental groups. This fibrewise holonomy is consistently interpreted as that of both Leray two-orientations and normalized Blattner--Kostant--Sternberg half-forms. The prequantizations pull back to flat circle bundles on each Lagrangian submanifold whose holonomy character defines a quantizability condition.
