The first and second Stiefel--Whitney classes are identified as splitting obstructions to the Lagrangianwise holonomies. These holonomies split into a product of holonomies on any orientable Lagrangian submanifold, and split consistently for all Lagrangian submanifolds of a manifold with metaplectic structure. When the first Chern class vanishes, the holonomy splits into the Bohr--Sommerfeld factor and a quarter phase Maslov correction, recovering the classical Einstein--Brillouin--Keller condition. We develop the underlying obstruction theory for circle extensions associated to general Lie group double coverings with first hypercohomology groupoids.
item.dc:creator: Hyunmoon Kim

item.title: Linking numbers and special differential characters in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.18503v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct non-holomorphic Siegel modular forms whose coefficients encode linking numbers in arithmetic hyperbolic manifolds of simplest type. Our proofs rely on an improved understanding of the transgression forms appearing in Kudla--Millson theory, and along the way we establish some structural properties including in particular their expected current equations.
item.dc:creator: Mads Bjerge Christensen

item.title: Generic boundary behavior of Dirichlet eigenfunctions
item.description: arXiv:2610.18619v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We extend Uhlenbeck's classical results on the generic properties of Laplacian eigenfunctions. In particular, we find a residual set of $C^k$ domains in $\mathbb{R}^n$, $k > n$, such that the nodal set of any Dirichlet eigenfunction intersects the boundary orthogonally along a $C^{k-1}$ embedded submanifold, whenever the intersection is non-empty. This is achieved by analyzing the boundary asymptotics of Dirichlet eigenfunctions via homogeneous harmonic polynomials and comparing their respective nodal sets. Along the way, we give a complete proof that generic Euclidean domains have simple Dirichlet eigenfunctions with zero as a regular value in the interior and zero as a regular value of the boundary normal derivative. In the special case of planar domains, a different argument provides one-parameter families of perturbed domains with the desired properties.
item.dc:creator: Alec Payne, Zihui Zhao

item.title: Generalized minimizers for the capillarity energy outside convex obstacles
item.description: arXiv:2610.18673v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In general, the capillarity energy outside an unbounded obstacle may fail to admit volume-constrained minimizers, as infimizing sequences may escape to infinity. We study this minimization problem outside a closed convex obstacle $C$. Via a $\Gamma$-convergence result for the capillarity energies outside sequences of closed convex obstacles converging in the Hausdorff sense, we prove that the infimum of the functional is attained by a generalized minimizer, namely, a finite union of regions, each of which minimizes the capillarity energy outside a limit of translations of $C$ in its volume class, with the total volume satisfying the prescribed constraint. Each generalized minimizer can be suitably approximated by an infimizing sequence, thus providing a description of its asymptotic behaviour. As an application, we study the isoperimetric profile associated with the capillarity energy and investigate how the asymptotic geometry of the obstacle affects both this profile and generalized minimizers and their connectedness.
item.dc:creator: Gabriele Nani, Simone Vincini

item.title: Complete $(2+1)$-dimensional Ricci flow spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2211.11866v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a complete $(2+1)$-dimensional Ricci flow spacetime, we show that every worldline persists until the terminal time of the flow, and that at each time, the collection of worldlines not yet present is scattered. Consequently, only countably many worldlines can have inception time strictly larger than the initial time of the flow. Under non-negative curvature, every spatial slice must be diffeomorphic to a fixed surface and the spacetime is isomorphic to a classical Ricci flow on this surface. As an application, for any two-dimensional Ricci soliton, the completeness of the metric forces completeness of its soliton vector field.
item.dc:creator: Luke T. Peachey

item.title: Injectivity and stability for the sub-Riemannian X-ray transform on H-type groups
item.description: arXiv:2312.00594v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove injectivity and a stability estimate for the X-ray transform along sub-Riemannian geodesics of $H$-type groups, a setting in which almost every geodesic carries conjugate points. The geodesics are helices labeled by a charge $\lambda$ valued in the dual of the center. We prove a Fourier slice theorem, which identifies the X-ray transform over geodesics with charge $\lambda$ as the restriction of the group Fourier transform to their visible frequencies, followed by an explicit multiplier. We characterize the sets of charges whose geodesics determine an integrable function, as exactly those whose visible frequencies are dense. In particular, when the center of the group has dimension at least two, charges of a single magnitude suffice provided their directions fill a great circle. Laguerre asymptotics on the spectrum of the normal operator at fixed charge yields a stability estimate at every nonzero visible frequency with the loss of exactly half a derivative in the sub-Laplacian, except on the first Heisenberg group. Finally, we prove that data limited to a band or a cap of charges determines all sufficiently high central frequencies of an unknown function.
item.dc:creator: Steven Flynn

item.title: A classification result for eternal mean convex flows of finite total curvature type
item.description: arXiv:2403.12020v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article we partially classify the space of eternal mean convex flows in $\mathbb{R}^3$ of finite total curvature type, a condition implied by finite total curvature. In particular we show that topologically nonplanar ones must flow out of a catenoid in a natural sense.
item.dc:creator: Alexander Mramor

item.title: Nonexistence of minimizers for the second conformal eigenvalue near the round sphere in low dimensions
item.description: arXiv:2408.07823v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider the problem of minimizing the second conformal eigenvalue of the conformal Laplacian in a conformal class of metrics with renormalized volume. We prove, in dimensions $n\in\left\{3,\dotsc,10\right\}$, that a minimizer for this problem does not exist for metrics sufficiently close to the round metric on the sphere. This is in striking contrast with the situation in dimensions $n \ge 11$, where Ammann and Humbert obtained the existence of minimizers for the second conformal eigenvalue on any smooth closed non-locally conformally flat manifold. As a byproduct of our techniques, we also obtain a lower bound on the energy of sign-changing solutions of the \nobreak Yamabe equation in dimensions 3, 4 and 5, which extends a result obtained by Weth in the case of the round sphere.
item.dc:creator: Bruno Premoselli, J\'er\^ome V\'etois

item.title: Stability of Minkowski-type inequalities in certain warped product spaces
item.description: arXiv:2505.06422v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper explores the stability of Minkowski-type inequalities for hypersurfaces in warped product spaces. We establish a stability estimate that bounds the norm of the traceless second fundamental form of the hypersurface in terms of the deficit in the Minkowski inequalities satisfied by the hypersurface. Additionally, we prove the stability of Minkowski inequalities in specific cases of the Reissner-Nordstr\"om Anti-de Sitter (RN-AdS) and Anti-de Sitter Schwarzschild (AdS-Schwarzschild) manifolds, which serve as examples of warped products. We also establish a new rigidity result for locally conformally flat manifolds to understand the stability of these inequalities.
item.dc:creator: Prachi Sahjwani

item.title: C'est un petit val qui mousse de fonctions
item.description: arXiv:2509.10574v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Easy lowering local minima, after introducing valley functions on smooth manifolds gives, without gluing technicities, "M. Morse's lemma's" canonical form, moving critical values and eliminating pair of critical points theorems, reducing the last to its one dimensional case.
item.dc:creator: Alexis Marin

item.title: Classification of the geodesic curves of the sub-Riemannian LR system on the Heisenberg group in dimension 5
item.description: arXiv:2512.11155v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study sub-Riemannian structures obtained by the restriction of the standard left-invariant Riemannian metric to a right-invariant completely nonholonomic distribution on the second Heisenberg group. The corresponding Hamiltonian system is completely integrable and in this paper we study its solutions. We obtain a complete classification of the geodesic curves by studying the reduced Hamiltonian system. Moreover, we compute $r(t)$ as the first step of the quadrature in the reduced system in the hyper-spherical coordinates and present numerical examples that illustrate the theoretical results.
item.dc:creator: Milan Pavlovi\'c

item.title: Scalar Curvature in Dimension 4
item.description: arXiv:2512.13528v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every locally conformally flat metric on a closed, oriented hyperbolic $4$-manifold with scalar curvature bounded below by $-12$ satisfies Schoen's conjecture. We also classify all closed, oriented Riemannian $4$-manifolds of positive scalar curvature that arise as total spaces of fiber bundles whose fiber and base are connected and have positive dimension and whose base is orientable. For a closed, locally conformally flat, scalar-flat manifold $(M^4,g)$ with $\pi_2(M^4) \neq 0$, we show that the universal Riemannian cover $(\widetilde{M},\tilde{g})$ is homothetic to the standard product $\mathbb{H}^2 \times S^2$. This affirmatively answers a question of M.~H.~Noronha.
item.dc:creator: Jialong Deng

item.title: Prescribing the mean curvature of an achronal hypersurface as a measure: the case of 3D spacetimes
item.description: arXiv:2512.17670v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the existence problem for achronal hypersurfaces $M \hookrightarrow \overline{M}$ in a globally hyperbolic spacetime, whose mean curvature is a prescribed -- possibly singular -- source, and whose boundary is a given smooth spacelike submanifold. Since $M$ is allowed to go null somewhere, the mean curvature prescription is to be understood in the distributional sense. We prove a general existence and regularity theorem for surfaces in ambient dimension $3$. Although most of our estimates hold in any dimension, recent counterexamples show that some of our conclusions fail in ambient dimension at least $5$. The case of $4$D-spacetimes is an open problem. Our theorems have application to Born-Infeld electrostatics in general static spacetimes.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Maniscalco, Luciano Mari

item.title: Homogeneous spaces with geodesic orbit Riemannian metrics and with integrable invariant distributions
item.description: arXiv:2601.07277v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We consider two types of homogeneous spaces of Lie groups with compact stabilizer subgroups: those with integrable invariant distributions and those for which all invariant Riemannian metrics are geodesic orbit. Recall that a Riemannian metric is called geodesic orbit if each geodesic is an orbit of a one-parameter subgroup of the full isometry group. We exhibit several homogeneous spaces of the first type that do not belong to the second one.
item.dc:creator: V. N. Berestovskii, Yu. G. Nikonorov

item.title: Geometric and topological rigidity of pinched submanifolds in Riemannian manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2602.17246v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the rigidity of compact submanifolds of arbitrary codimension in Riemannian manifolds satisfying a pinching condition involving the norm of the second fundamental form and the mean curvature. In contrast to the corresponding earlier results, the pinching condition is not required to hold strictly. Allowing equality gives rise to richer and subtler geometric and topological phenomena. By analyzing the nonstrict boundary case in arbitrary ambient manifolds, we obtain a classification of the possible intrinsic geometries and topologies of the submanifold, together with restrictions on its extrinsic geometry. We also provide several families of examples satisfying the pinching condition, showing that the conclusions cannot, in general, be strengthened to extrinsic rigidity statements. The resulting theorems extend several known results in the literature, particularly sphere theorems, to the nonstrict setting while removing several additional geometric or topological assumptions appearing in earlier results.
item.dc:creator: Theodoros Vlachos

item.title: Nonlinear Lebesgue spaces: Curves and geometry
item.description: arXiv:2603.09459v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper is the second in a series by the author and collaborators devoted to the study of geometric and analytic properties of nonlinear Lebesgue spaces, that is, L^p spaces of mappings taking values in arbitrary metric spaces. The present article formalizes the pointwise description of their geometric properties---their length structure, bounds on their Alexandrov curvature as well as the definition of a velocity for absolutely continuous curves despite the lack of differential structure. To obtain this pointwise description, we first prove a nonlinear analogue of the Fubini--Lebesgue theorem, which yields an identification of L^p curves in nonlinear Lebesgue spaces with mappings taking values in the space of L^p curves. This identification of L^p curves then enables a similar identification for absolutely continuous curves, from which the pointwise description of the geometric properties of nonlinear Lebesgue spaces follows.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume S\'erieys (MAP5 - UMR 8145)

item.title: Curvature equivalence for Legendre curves in the unit tangent bundle over Euclidean plane
item.description: arXiv:2604.07898v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Legendre curve in the unit tangent bundle over Euclidean plane is a plane curve with a moving frame. We have the (Legendre) curvature of the Legendre curve, and the existence and uniqueness theorems for the curvature are valid. In this paper, we introduce an equivalence relation for Legendre curves called the curvature equivalence. We investigate properties of the curvature equivalence and give local and global classifications of Legendre curves under the curvature equivalence.
item.dc:creator: Nozomi Nakatsuyama, Masatomo Takahashi, Minoru Yamamoto

item.title: A Geometric Interpretation of Generalized Hurwitz--Radon Numbers Defined by Kannaka--Tojo
item.description:
arXiv:2605.00704v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Hurwitz--Radon number originates in the composition problem of quadratic forms and is related to the maximum number of pointwise linearly independent vector fields on spheres. Kannaka--Tojo [arXiv:2602.04544] reformulated the Hurwitz--Radon number in the setting of a real reductive Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ and its faithful representation $\iota$, and introduced two natural numbers $ho^{(1)}(\mathfrak g,\iota)$ and $ho^{(2)}(\mathfrak g,\iota)$. For classical Lie algebras and their standard representations, these two numbers coincide except for a few cases. In this paper, fixing a Lie group $G$ and a subspace $\mathfrak{s} $ of $ \mathfrak g = \operatorname{Lie}(G)$ , we define natural numbers $ho_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,\sigma)$ and $ho^{\pm}_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,\sigma,
abla)$ for a $G$-manifold $(M,\sigma)$ equipped with an affine connection $
abla$. These are defined in terms of fundamental vector fields on $M$. In a special case, we show that $ho_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,\sigma)$ coincides with $ho^{(2)}(\mathfrak g,\iota)$, and that $ho^{-}_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,\sigma,
abla)$ coincides with $ho^{(1)}(\mathfrak g,\iota)$. Furthermore, we show that $ho^{+}_{G,\mathfrak{s}}(M,\sigma,
abla)$ is related to Clifford structures on $M$.
item.dc:creator: Muneto Miyaji

item.title: Cohomogeneity-One Ruled Hypersurfaces in $\mathbb{CP}^2$ and $\mathbb{C}H^2$
item.description: arXiv:2605.22979v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we show how to construct a special class of ruled hypersurfaces in the nonflat complex space forms $\mathbb{CP}^n$ and $\mathbb{C}H^n$. This is done by taking an arbitrary smooth curve in a totally geodesic (complex) one-dimensional submanifold and erecting an orthogonal ruling over each of its points. Concentrating on the $n=2$ case, we also examine the special situation in which the base curve has constant geodesic curvature. We show that, in this case, the construction yields precisely the real-analytic hypersurfaces of cohomogeneity one that satisfy a certain transversality condition.
item.dc:creator: Thomas A. Ivey, Patrick J. Ryan

item.title: Godbillon-Vey classes of Lie subalgebroids
item.description: arXiv:2606.27340v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Godbillon--Vey class is a secondary characteristic class which is defined for regular foliations and has been studied extensively. In this paper, we fix a Lie algebroid and relatively define the Godbillon--Vey class for its Lie subalgebroids, and study their properties. We also present several examples.
item.dc:creator: Shuhei Yonehara

item.title: A Bernstein Theorem for the Self-Shrinking $J$-Equation and Some Generalizations
item.description: arXiv:2606.29546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every entire smooth strictly plurisubharmonic solution of the self-shrinking $J$-equation on $\mathbb{C}^n$ is a quadratic polynomial. This removes the asymptotic lower bound assumption on the complex Hessian in \cite[Theorem 4]{HJ}. The result also recovers the corresponding real rigidity theorem in \cite[Theorem 1.1]{HOW} as a special case. More generally, our method applies to self-shrinking equations associated with a broad class of fully nonlinear elliptic operators satisfying suitable structural conditions, including the adjacent inverse complex Hessian quotient operators $-\sigma_{k-1}/\sigma_{k}$, $1\leq k\leq n$. For the remaining quotients $-\sigma_l/\sigma_k$ with $l<k-1$, we prove the same rigidity conclusion under the additional assumption that the solution is proper.
item.dc:creator: Yiyang Pan, Wenlong Wang

item.title: Pr\"ufer $2$-group and Milnor's Conjecture on Fundamental Groups
item.description: arXiv:2608.15505v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct complete, one-ended Riemannian manifolds in dimensions four and five having strictly positive Ricci curvature, with fundamental group isomorphic to the Pr\"ufer $2$-group $C_{2^\infty}$ and any subgroup $\Gamma\leq \mathbb Q/\mathbb Z$, respectively. This gives counterexamples to Milnor's conjecture in the two remaining dimensions.
item.dc:creator: Nan Wu, Zetian Yan

item.title: Comparison between renormalized volume and area in the Weil--Petersson topology
item.description: arXiv:2609.03723v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the renormalized volume between the two Epstein surfaces associated with a Weil--Petersson quasicircle is continuous with respect to the Weil--Petersson topology. As a consequence, we establish that the universal Liouville action is proportional to this renormalized volume for every Weil--Petersson quasicircle. We then establish an inequality relating this renormalized volume to the renormalized area introduced by Alexakis--Mazzeo. To this end, we compare both quantities with the Hilbert--Schmidt norm of the associated Grunsky operator, which can be expressed in terms of a nonlocal Lagrangian introduced by O'Hara--Solanes.
item.dc:creator: Dorian Martino

item.title: Rigidity and volume pinching for the sharp gradient estimate in positive Ricci curvature
item.description: arXiv:2609.03739v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Colding established a sharp gradient estimate for the Green function on manifolds with non-negative Ricci curvature, which was extended to positive Ricci curvature by Manea recently. We prove almost rigidity of such gradient estimates for positive Ricci curvature. We show that the average of the gradient deficit, namely $\fint (1-|\nabla b|^2)\,dV$, controls the volume deficit in an optimal quantitative manner; here $b$ is the distance-like function defined using the Green function. This implies a quantitative almost rigidity theorem for manifolds with $\ric\ge(n-1)g$ and a gap theorem for Einstein manifolds. We also prove a rigidity theorem for closed 4-dimensional Einstein manifolds by finding a new monotonicity formula.
item.dc:creator: Junyoung Kim, Jiewon Park

item.title: Rigidity, sharp inequalities, and stability for $\sigma_2$-curvature by a reference curvature technique
item.description: arXiv:2609.10523v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Using a reference-curvature technique, we prove four main theorems. (i) For $n\geq4$, we remove the mean-curvature pinching from the Case-Wang rigidity theorem for $\sigma_2$-flat conformal hemispheres with $A_g\in\overline{\Gamma_2^+}$ and positive constant natural boundary curvature. (ii) On every closed positive Einstein manifold of dimension $n\geq5$, each conformal metric of constant $\sigma_2$-curvature is Einstein, and is homothetic to the background unless the background is a round sphere, thereby resolving the $\sigma_2$-Obata problem posed by Chang, Gursky, and Yang. (iii) We extend the spherical constant-$\sigma_2/\sigma_1$ classification and sharp integral comparison to closed positive Einstein manifolds. The comparison holds throughout the positive-scalar-curvature conformal class, with equality only for homotheties on nonround backgrounds. (iv) We establish global quantitative $\sigma_2$ stability on every fixed nonround positive Einstein background of dimension $n\geq5$, throughout its positive-scalar-curvature conformal class.
item.dc:creator: Wangzhe Wu

item.title: Morse Index of a $G_2$-Instanton over $S^7$
item.description: arXiv:2609.14369v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we determine the nonpositive spectrum of the Yang-Mills Jacobi operator in Coulomb gauge at the standard $G_2$-instanton on $S^7$. We prove that the only negative eigenvalue is $-3$, with multiplicity $8$, and the kernel has dimension $20$. Thus the connection attains the sharp lower bound for the Morse index of nonflat Yang-Mills connections on $S^7$. We also give an explicit description of the kernal of the Jacobi operator, which contains Waldron's $15$-dimensional deformation space for the fixed nearly parallel $G_2$-structure. The 5 additional zero modes are isometry-induced variations that do not satisfy the corresponding linearized instanton equation.
item.dc:creator: Xiaoli Han, Yang Wen

item.title: A concise proof of homogeneity of an isoparametric hypersurface with $(g, m)=(6, 2)$
item.description: arXiv:2609.16658v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A well-known hypersurface classification theorem states that any isoparametric hypersurface in $S^{13}$ with six principal curvatures is homogeneous. This landmark result was first proved in her Annals paper in 2013 by R. Miyaoka with 58 pages, and with errata in Annals in 2016 with 15 pages. The main purpose of this paper is to provide a concise proof of this theorem through an interplay between topological and geometric insights into the Euler class of an oriented vector bundle.
item.dc:creator: Chao Qian, Zizhou Tang

item.title: Laplacian Algebras and Subcalibrations for Minimal Hypercones
item.description: arXiv:2609.17217v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We develop an algebraic mechanism based on Laplacian algebras for constructing minimal hypercones and determining their variational properties. Generator counts and degrees organize the constructions; homogeneous multipliers depending on the generators yield subcalibration fields, stability bounds and quantitative area-minimizing inequalities. Two-generator isoparametric algebras give polynomial subcalibrations for their minimizing hypercones. In ambient dimension at least three, strict gradient-square closure forces nonlinear odd degree to be cubic. We then study algebras of degrees $(2,2,g)$ and quadratic compositions, placing OT--FKM splitting quartics and Riedler's pullbacks in a common quadratic-composition framework. It yields two further infinite quartic families with a sharp minimizing threshold, as well as harmonic sextics from complex Gram coordinates. For an irreducible harmonic minimal cubic on its essential space, we prove a sharp bound of five generators for its smallest Laplacian algebra. We determine the minimizing range of Clifford cubics and construct irreducible nonradial harmonic examples in ambient dimensions $8,14,26$; the last is strictly area minimizing. Finally, spectral families whose smallest algebras have arbitrarily many generators provide examples in every degree at least two: real parts of octonionic products, complex Pfaffians and complex determinants. Explicit potentials establish strict area minimality and stability bounds, including across nonisolated singularities. The algebraic identities and certificates are supported by reproducible exact symbolic computations.
item.dc:creator: Hongbin Cui

item.title: A diameter gap for irreducible compact symmetric spaces of fixed rank
item.description: arXiv:2609.21535v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that, for every positive integer $r$, the positive normalized diameters of isometric quotients of simply connected irreducible compact Riemannian symmetric spaces of rank $r$ have a uniform positive lower bound. The bound is independent of the dimension and of the acting group, which need not be connected. For the higher-dimensional Grassmannian families, we obtain an explicit bound for positive-dimensional acting groups by constructing nonconstant invariant functions of bounded trigonometric degree. The real and complex cases use moment maps. The quaternionic case follows from a quartic rigidity theorem proved by means of invariant four-forms and the classification of compact quaternionic symmetric spaces. We also give examples showing why the rank and the relative scales of product factors must be controlled.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqi Chen, Shaoqiang Deng, Hui Zhang

item.title: Conformal Killing--Yano Ricci solitons: Structure, compatibility, and rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2609.23424v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We introduce a geometric structure -- a conformal Killing--Yano Ricci soliton (CKY--RS) -- that couples conformal Ricci soliton (CRS) geometry to conformal Killing--Yano (CKY) 2--forms. The soliton field of the CRS geometry is given by the divergence of the CKY 2--form. We introduce a conserved CKY--Cotton current and derive a compatibility identity relating the Cotton tensor, the CRS obstruction tensor, and the CKY 2--form. In 4--dimensional Lorentzian signature, we show that, under non-degeneracy and closedness assumptions on the CKY form, a CKY--RS structure forces the conformal representative to be locally Kerr--NUT--(A)dS. For a closed non-degenerate CKY on a Kerr--NUT--(A)dS background, the conformal deformation is necessarily trivial. For Einstein backgrounds of arbitrary dimension and signature, the conformal factor satisfies an eigenvalue equation and an Obata--type Hessian equation. If the background is also compact or a CKY orbit is periodic, the conformal factor is an invariant of the CKY--flow and we obtain simple spectral obstructions to non-trivial CKY--RS structures. From the Hessian equation, we obtain obstruction and classification results for the non-trivial conformal sector, including product/Brinkmann geometries and a Weyl--aligned branch. Finally, we give explicit constructions for static spherically symmetric geometries and BTZ backgrounds, including a CKY--RS realization with a time-dependent conformally flat representative. These results provide a geometric framework for studying CRS with hidden symmetry structure, with potential applications to exact geometries in general relativity.
item.dc:creator: Mohammadjavad Habibivostakolaei, Abbas M. Sherif, Yen-Kheng Lim

item.title: Chern Holomorphic Sectional Curvature: Canonical Ampleness, Rigidity, and Flatness Counterexamples
item.description: arXiv:2609.25762v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the relation between canonical positivity, rigidity of a prescribed Hermitian metric, and the curvature not detected by Chern holomorphic sectional curvature. A compact Brody-hyperbolic complex manifold admitting an independent smooth plurinegative Hermitian metric is projective with ample canonical bundle. In Fujiki's class, nonpositive constant Chern holomorphic sectional curvature forces the original metric to be K\"ahler. On compact complex threefolds, without an auxiliary metric or a Fujiki-class assumption, a nonzero constant forces K\"ahlerness. We also give an alternative proof of Chen--Zheng's Chern-flatness theorem for zero-HSC threefolds, by proving local rank-two differential compatibility and localizing their curvature bound under $\partial\eta=0$. In contrast, for every complex dimension at least seven we give compact balanced zero-HSC metrics with nonzero Chern curvature. Their octonionic curvature formula also implies the vanishing of all four Chern--Ricci contractions, and an explicit invariant volume form is Chern parallel. Finally, an auxiliary semipositive plurinegative $(1,1)$-form, positive definite at some point, restores flat K\"ahlerness under zero HSC and vanishing first Chern--Ricci tensor. A mixed Ricci integral criterion explains the role of this last curvature hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Xiangsen Qin, Yuanhong Tian

item.title: Timelike surfaces of constant mean and constant Gaussian curvature in anti-de Sitter 3-space via loop groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.33504v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The loop group description of surfaces whose Gauss map is Lorentz harmonic is known for timelike surfaces of constant mean curvature in the flat Lorentzian 3-space, and for surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature in the 3-sphere. We carry out the corresponding construction for timelike surfaces in anti-de Sitter 3-space $\mathbb{H}^3_1\cong SL(2,\mathbb{R})$: those of constant mean curvature, whose Gauss map is harmonic for the conformal structure of the first fundamental form, and those of constant Gaussian curvature $K>-1$, $K\neq0$, whose Gauss map is then an immersion and is harmonic for the second fundamental form. For both classes we prove the harmonicity characterization, recover the surfaces from extended frames by Sym-Bobenko-type formulas, and solve the geometric Cauchy problem by the generalized DPW method, with potentials written explicitly in terms of the data and no normalization of the Gauss map. We then show that the two constructions differ only by a normalization: after the substitution $\lambda=\zeta^2$ and a constant gauge, a constant mean curvature extended frame $\hat F$ is an extended frame of its Gauss map, and the maps $\hat F|_{\lambda=e^{4\theta}}\exp(\theta e_3)\hat F|_{\lambda=1}^{-1}$ and $e_3\hat F|_{\lambda=e^{4\theta}}e_3\exp(\theta e_3)\hat F|_{\lambda=1}^{-1}$, with $e_3=\mathrm{diag}(-1,1)$, are timelike surfaces of constant Gaussian curvature $1/\sinh^2\theta$ and $-1/\cosh^2\theta$ wherever the constant mean curvature surface is not flat. The first is the classical parallel surface, the second its polar surface. Explicit families, with extended frames and surfaces in closed form, illustrate the constructions.
item.dc:creator: Jorge Bravo-Gadea

item.title: Derived deformation theory of heterotic $G_2$ systems near the standard embedding
item.description: arXiv:2609.35071v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study heterotic $G_2$ structures near a torsion-free standard embedding, to first order in $\alpha'$ and to all orders in formal deformations. The tangent connection is the Hull connection determined by the metric and flux. We construct a locally invertible family of differential operators relating the supersymmetry and instanton $BPS$ equations to the Euler-Lagrange equations of the heterotic superpotential. Using this comparison and the physical gauge symmetries, we construct a homological vector field locally formally conjugate to the Hamiltonian vector field of the superpotential. On a closed manifold in the fixed gerbe sector, the torsion equation implies vanishing of the leading flux. We prove ellipticity of the linearized deformation complex with mixed differential-order weights and construct a finite-dimensional cyclic $L_\infty$ model with a formal effective potential.
item.dc:creator: Bram Brongers

item.title: A geometric rigidity estimate for codimension-1 immersions into spheres
item.description: arXiv:2609.37665v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a quantitative stability estimate for codimension-one immersions into a round sphere. Let $(M,g)$ be an oriented Riemannian manifold and suppose that a prescribed shape operator is realised by a smooth isometric immersion $\theta:(M,g)\to\mathbb S^{n+1}$. We prove that, on every relatively compact strongly Lipschitz domain and for every $1<p<\infty$, any Sobolev immersion $\phi$ is close to $\theta$ modulo an ambient rotation, with the $W^{1,p}$-distances between both the immersions and their Gauss maps controlled by the $L^p$ stretching-plus-bending energies of $\phi$. No {\it a priori} bounds on the fundamental forms of $\phi$ are required. The proof proceeds by extending the immersions along normal geodesics and reducing the problem to an equidimensional geometric rigidity estimate on the sphere. A finite localisation and patching argument handles the possible non-injectivity of the normal extension of the reference immersion.
item.dc:creator: Siran Li, Isaac Newell

item.title: Steady gradient Ricci Yang-Mills solitons on 2-orbifolds
item.description: arXiv:2609.38773v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Following the recent work of M. Womack \cite{Wo26} we consider the steady Ricci Yang-Mills solitons on 2d surfaces containing orbifold point $\mathbb{R}^2/\mathbb{Z}_p$. We show that there are a family of solitons depending parameter $\lambda$ which approaches to $\mathbb{Z}_p$-quotient of Hamilton cigar soliton as $\lambda \to (-2/p)^+$ and approaches to (after rescaling) $\mathbb{Z}_p$-quotient of round sphere as $\lambda \to \infty$. For any integer $q >p$ there is a $\lambda$ whose corresponding soliton metric is defined on football orbifold $S_{p,q}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Peng Lu, Jiuru Zhou

item.title: On the Morse index of nonorientable minimal surfaces in $\mathbb{R}^3$
item.description: arXiv:2609.40074v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We compute the Morse index of several complete nonorientable minimal surfaces immersed in Euclidean three-space. In particular, we prove that the Meeks minimal M\"obius band has Morse index two, which is the least possible Morse index for such nonorientable minimal surfaces, by previous works of Ros and Chodosh-Maximo. This is the first known minimal surface with index two. We show that the L\'opez minimal Klein bottle has Morse index three. As a consequence of this computation, we extend results in the literature and observe that any complete minimal surface immersed in Euclidean three-space with total curvature $8 \pi$ has Morse index three. We also compute the Morse index of the Oliveira family of minimal M\"obius bands in terms of their total curvature and show that every non-negative integer is the Morse index of a complete minimal surface immersed in Euclidean three-space. We show that five is a sharp lower bound for the Morse index of any minimal oriented double cover in Euclidean three-space, and equality is attained by the double cover of the Meeks minimal M\"obius band. Finally, we prove results towards the classification of complete minimal surfaces with Morse index two immersed in Euclidean three-space, obtaining topological and geometric restrictions on such surfaces.
item.dc:creator: Carlos Andr\'es Toro Cardona, Carlos Granada-Palacio, Ivan Miranda

item.title: Positive sectional curvature on homotopy nine-spheres
item.description: arXiv:2610.03298v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine which homotopy nine-spheres admit positive sectional curvature: they are precisely the four smooth types with vanishing real Dirac index. The other four admit no metric of nonnegative sectional curvature. In particular, we construct a strictly positively curved metric on the exotic Kervaire nine-sphere, answering the longstanding nonnegative-curvature existence question in this dimension. The proof keeps explicit attaching maps throughout. A quaternionic commutator realizes the Kervaire sphere, a mixed representation realizes the Hopf image of the exotic eight-sphere, and a four-periodic normal-framing formula identifies the remaining index-zero class. Following the compatible-disk method, we give the curvature and boundary estimates for the first two models, including an explicit lower bound for the Kervaire metric in terms of the curvature and first covariant-derivative norms of a fixed connection, with the base scale and fiber normalization fixed. For the third model, we construct a positive metric on a cylinder joining a quotient metric to its pullback by a marked right Hopf twist. A four-form modification controls the connection terms involving both left and right quaternionic multiplication. Two positive disk fillings close the cylinder with the prescribed attaching map. A local convolution lemma supplies the smooth gluing while preserving a strict sectional-curvature lower bound.
item.dc:creator: Zhiqi Chen, Shaoqiang Deng, Junna Ni, Hui Zhang

item.title: Nahm-Kirchhoff Moduli Spaces, Hyperk\"ahler Quotient and 2D Field theories
item.description: arXiv:2610.03384v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: To an oriented quiver with boundary $\Gamma$ and a compact connected Lie group $G$ we associate a Nahm-Kirchhoff moduli space $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{H}}(\Gamma)$: solutions of Nahm's equations on the edges with Kirchhoff matching at interior vertices, modulo boundary-trivial gauge transformations. For connected $\Gamma$, $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{H}}(\Gamma)$ is a smooth manifold of dimension $4(|E|-|\Gamma_{\mathrm{int}}|)\dim G$ with a hyperk\"ahler structure arising as an infinite-dimensional hyperk\"ahler quotient. Via a Kempf-Ness argument on the Cartan-Hadamard manifold $G_{\mathbb{C}}/G$, we prove a quiver analogue of Donaldson's theorem identifying it with the complex-symplectic quotient $\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}}(\Gamma)$ of the complex Nahm equations by the complexified gauge group. This quotient is independent of edge lengths and isomorphic to a finite-dimensional complex-symplectic quotient of $(T^*G_{\mathbb{C}})^E$, while the hyperk\"ahler metric depends on them: uniform rescaling acts by a homothety, and the transported metrics genuinely vary. By cutting and gluing, $\Gamma\mapsto\mathcal{M}_{\mathbb{C}}(\Gamma)$ is a 2D TQFT valued in complex Hamiltonian manifolds, \`a la Moore-Tachikawa, whereas the hyperk\"ahler refinement is not functorial on $\mathbf{Cob}_2$: spines of a cylinder with different lengths give non-isomorphic spaces. Retaining lengths, these spaces form a metric field theory, a functor of non-unital monoidal categories from metric cobordisms to hyperk\"ahler manifolds composed by hyperk\"ahler reduction; over each cone of $M_{g,n}^{\mathrm{trop}}$ they give a family with fixed complex-symplectic fibre and varying metric. Finally, harmonic gauge representatives converge as an internal edge collapses, and on a long edge with regular semisimple Higgs field the Kempf-Ness minimizer is exponentially confined near its centralizer; the limiting metrics are left open.
item.dc:creator: Mohamed Moussadek Maiza

item.title: Analyticity and tautness of smooth Dupin hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.04679v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that smooth immersed Dupin submanifolds of Euclidean space are locally Nash in arbitrary codimension and that every compact embedded Dupin submanifold is taut. These conclusions follow from our hypersurface results by the tube construction. For hypersurfaces, we require the Dupin condition only where the principal multiplicities are locally constant. No local finiteness assumption on this regular locus, or regularity assumption on its complement, is required. The proof combines a dimension-dependent degree bound on proper Dupin pieces with a continuation argument using finite jets and resultants. An analytic Hessian criterion then implies that all squared distance functions are Morse-Bott, and hence that every compact embedded hypersurface in this class is taut. In each dimension there are only finitely many such hypersurfaces up to Nash isotopy through embedded Dupin hypersurfaces. We also obtain finiteness results for taut submanifolds in arbitrary codimension and derive topological restrictions from classical classification theorems for taut embeddings.
item.dc:creator: Stephan Wiesendorf

item.title: Characterization of Sasakian Manifolds by Curvature Conditions
item.description: arXiv:2610.06463v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Sasakian manifolds, a subclass of contact metric manifolds, play a central role in modern differential geometry and mathematical physics, where they arise naturally in geometric mechanics, CR geometry, and supersymmetric field theories. The weak contact metric (w.c.m.) structure generalizes the contact metric structure and provides a broader framework for studying contact geometry and its applications. A fundamental problem is to understand how curvature conditions constrain the underlying contact metric structure and, in particular, how they distinguish Sasakian geometry from its weaker variants. Using the partial Ricci flow, we characterize Sasakian structure (among w.c.m. manifolds) under the $(\kappa,\mu)$-nullity condition related to curvature. For $\kappa<1$ we find conditions under which a w.c.m. manifold admits a bi-Legendrian structure, and for $\kappa=\mu=0$ establish splitting and classification results.
item.dc:creator: Sourav Nayak, Vladimir Rovenski, Dhriti Sundar Patra

item.title: Uniformly Positive Scalar Curvature on Manifold Interiors
item.description: arXiv:2610.07608v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We obtain topological obstructions to the existence of a complete Riemannian metric with uniformly positive scalar curvature on the interiors of certain 4-manifolds using Seiberg--Witten theory. In particular, no punctured blowups of a homotopy K3 manifold admit complete metrics of uniformly positive scalar curvature. Further, let $X$ be a compact oriented smooth manifold of dimension $5$, $6$, or $7$. We show that if $\operatorname{Int}X$ admits a complete metric of uniformly positive scalar curvature, then $X$ admits a positive scalar curvature metric with minimal boundary. In dimensions $6$ and $7$, the metric may moreover be chosen to be a product near the boundary. In dimension 5, under additional hypotheses and after possibly changing the smooth structure on $X$, one can likewise obtain a positive scalar curvature metric that is a product near the boundary.
item.dc:creator: Shuli Chen

item.title: Higher localised $\widehat{A}$-genera: a note on disconnected fixed-point sets
item.description: arXiv:2610.07833v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a proper cocompact action of a finitely generated discrete group $\Gamma$ on a spin manifold $M$, the higher localised $\widehat{A}$-genera $\widehat{A}_g(M,\omega)$ introduced earlier by the author and Mathai were shown to be an obstruction to $\Gamma$-invariant metrics of positive scalar curvature, for $\omega$ arising from the subring of $H^*(\underline{B}\Gamma,\mathbb{R})$ generated by elements of degree at most $2$, under the assumptions that the fixed-point set $M^g$ is connected and that $g$ is regular with respect to a certain real group $2$-cocycle. We show that both assumptions can be dropped.
item.dc:creator: Hao Guo

item.title: Einstein metrics with torus symmetry on $S^4$ and $\mathbb R^4$
item.description: arXiv:2610.12210v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This note gives direct proofs that, under an effective isometric $T^2$ action, Einstein metrics on smooth homotopy four-spheres are round and complete Ricci-flat metrics on smooth manifolds homeomorphic to $\mathbb R^4$ are Euclidean or positive one-center Taub--NUT, up to isometry, scaling, and orientation reversal.
item.dc:creator: Xiuxiong Chen, Conghan Dong

item.title: Auerbach bases of real $\ell_p^n$ spaces
item.description: arXiv:2302.00664v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study Auerbach bases of the space $\ell^n_p$, and in particular, prove that $\ell_p^n$ has only finitely many Auerbach bases for $p>n$ and $1<p<n/(n-1)$. An explicit one-parameter family in $\ell_4^4$ shows that the condition $p>n$ cannot in general be weakened to $p\geq n$. Further, we provide an explicit classification of the Auerbach bases in dimension two and three.
item.dc:creator: Arun Maiti, Debmalya Sain

item.title: Conformal hyperbolic distances and holonomies of Anosov diffeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2410.15740v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We use conformal hyperbolic distances to analyze the stable/unstable holonomies of Anosov diffeomorphisms. The main result is that the lengths of the stable/unstable curves in a conformal hyperbolic distance are preserved by the stable/unstable holonomies, whenever they are well-defined. In particular, the existence of a conformal hyperbolic distance with well-defined length of stable/unstable curves ensures that the holonomies are globally defined. We exhibit a conformal hyperbolic distance with well-defined length of stable/unstable curves for each real Anosov diffeomorphism, which are Anosov diffeomorphisms with a one-dimensional finest dominated splitting where contraction/expansion in each space is constant along orbits.
item.dc:creator: Bernardo Carvalho

item.title: Notes on Correlation Stress Tests
item.description: arXiv:2503.16200v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This note outlines an approach to stress testing of covariance of financial time series, in the context of financial risk management. It discusses how the geodesic distance between covariance matrices implies a notion of plausibility of covariance stress tests. In this approach, correlation stress tests span a submanifold of constant determinant of the Fisher--Rao manifold of covariance matrices. A parsimonious geometrically invariant definition of arbitrarily large correlation stress tests is proposed, and a few examples are discussed.
item.dc:creator: Piotr Chmielowski

item.title: Connectedness properties of small minimal clusters in Riemannian or Finsler manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2504.20587v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that in a compact Riemannian manifold, the $m$-minimal clusters of sufficiently small total volume are connected and with small diameter, while in a more general Finsler manifold they are done by at most $m$ connected components of small diameter. We apply these results to calculate the asymptotic expansion of the multi-isoperimetric profile at the first nontrivial order, for small volumes.
item.dc:creator: Stefano Nardulli, Aldo Pratelli

item.title: Jets of flat partial connections
item.description: arXiv:2505.11662v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We define and study jets of flat partial connections in the setting of smooth foliations and flat partial connections on locally free sheaves. In the case of codimension one foliations, we apply this definition to characterize transversely affine and transversely projective structures. For foliations of arbitrary codimension, we use jets of the Bott connection on the normal sheaf to define the prolongation of a transversely projective structure, and then apply it to produce singular transversely projective structures.
item.dc:creator: Gabriel Fazoli

item.title: Autoregressive Processes on Stiefel and Grassmann Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2509.24767v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: System identification methods for autoregressive processes on Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds are presented and studied. We model the system parameters as elements of the orthogonal group and we show that the system can be estimated by averaging over observations. Lastly, we propose an algorithm for computing these system parameters using a conjugate gradient method adapted to Stiefel and Grassmann manifolds.
item.dc:creator: Jordi-Llu\'is Figueras, Aron Persson

item.title: Properness and finiteness of totally geodesic submanifolds in the convex core
item.description: arXiv:2511.09377v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study totally geodesic submanifolds in the convex core of geometrically finite rank-one locally symmetric manifolds. Although the infinite-volume setting can exhibit highly complicated behavior, including geodesic planes with fractal closures, we show that a strong rigidity persists inside the convex core. This rigidity has striking consequences in the infinite volume setting: every maximal totally geodesic submanifold of dimension at least two contained in the convex core is properly immersed and has finite volume, and only finitely many such submanifolds can occur. These results stand in sharp contrast to the behavior in the finite-volume setting. Moreover, combining this finiteness result with the work of Bader-Fisher-Miller-Stover and of Gromov-Schoen, we deduce that any geometrically finite rank-one manifold with infinitely many maximal totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two and of finite volume must be arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Minju Lee, Hee Oh

item.title: Heat Kernel and Resurgence
item.description: arXiv:2606.21909v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the resurgent structure of short--time heat kernel asymptotics from the viewpoint of Picard--Lefschetz theory. For a real analytic Riemannian manifold, we show the heat kernel admits a 1-- Gevrey small--time expansion whose Borel transform detects complex--geometric data beyond the real geodesic sector. We formulate an infinite--dimensional Picard--Lefschetz problem of Morse--Floer type for the holomorphic energy functional on the complexified path space, and propose a heat--kernel analogue of the Picard--Lefschetz/Alien correspondence. In this framework, pointed alien operators acting on the asymptotic expansion associated with the real geodesic are predicted to produce the formal heat--kernel sectors associated with other holomorphic geodesics, with coefficients given by signed counts of connecting trajectories of the Morse flow. We perform a confirming test of this proposal on the hyperbolic plane $\mathbb{H}_{\R}^2$.
item.dc:creator: Si Li, Yong Li, Xinxing Tang

item.title: Beyond Cultural Persona Bias: Response Geometry as a Measure for Language Models and People
item.description: arXiv:2607.02368v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Researchers are increasingly prompting language models with cultural personas so that they answer questionnaires as diverse human groups would. However, studies often report that these persona responses do not predict the models' behavior. We argue that whether the persona is Western or non-Western, the model's answers carry a cultural preference, and that this preference masks the variables that could predict its behavior. We examine the prompted preference at two levels: aggregate Big Five scores and response geometry, the correlation matrix between dimensions within each respondent, represented as a symmetric positive-definite (SPD) matrix. In DeepSeek-V3 and GPT-4o, when the item order is fixed, the prompted preference appears at both levels. Randomizing item order reduces it in the response geometry, while leaving it in the Big Five scores: the Big Five still separate the two personas at $95$--$97\%$, while response geometry falls to chance. In randomized administration, the response geometry still contains information about the respondent. In DeepSeek-V4-Flash, SPD features are associated with whether the same instance sorts Asian American public figures as ``foreign'' in a text IAT ($p = .047$), while the Big Five do not. In human studies conducted using randomized item order, the response geometry identifies people from test-retest sessions in $81$ -- $85\%$, against chance $0.4\%$, and predicts sex and, weakly, age. In addition, SPD features also predict complex human behavior (e.g., cumulative GPA, $R^2 = 0.28$, permutation $p = .003$), where the Big Five do not.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yuan

item.title: Conformal Renormalisation of 8D Einstein Gravity
item.description: arXiv:2607.03679v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that Holographic Renormalisation (HR) in eight dimensions is encoded in the unique conformal gravity theory that admits an Einstein sector with constant negative curvature. We explicitly relate HR to Topological Regularisation (TR), where the latter prescribes to add the Euler term to the Einstein-Hilbert Lagrangian density, with a precise coefficient so as to ensure that the resulting density is polynomial in the anti de Sitter (AdS) curvature. The polynomial is still asymptotically divergent. We find that the aforementioned, unique conformal gravity action in 8D, reproduces the polynomial, together with extra boundary terms that cancel the divergent terms in the action. We conjecture that, in arbitrary even dimension, HR is equivalent to conformally completing the Einstein-Hilbert action with negative cosmological constant, plus the Euler term with fixed coupling prescribed by TR.
item.dc:creator: Giorgos Anastasiou, Ignacio J. Araya, Nicolas Boulanger, Rodrigo Olea, Davide Rovere

item.title: Graphon as a Bridge between Graphs and Manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2607.20213v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that there exist graphons that interpolate between Riemannian manifolds and weighted geometric graphs. Specifically, the graph-to-manifold approximation used in manifold learning can be regarded as the composition of a graph-to-graphon convergence and a graphon-to-manifold convergence in a certain sense. Furthermore, we establish a monotonicity inequality which reveals an implicit relationship between numerous combinatorial parameters and geometric quantities on graphons. Using this inequality, we find relations among conductance, maxcut problem, capacity, and packing radius, as well as their limiting behaviors under graph-to-graphon and graphon-to-manifold convergences; some of these relations are novel even for simple graphs and closed manifolds. We also find that in the graphon-to-manifold limiting process, the purely combinatorial parameters diverge, leading to a ``blowup'' phenomenon; and continuous versions of some graph parameters cannot be realized via Riemannian manifolds, but can be realized via graphons.
item.dc:creator: Dong Zhang

item.title: A nonlinear Li-Yau inequality and its consequences
item.description:
arXiv:2608.28881v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove a sharp nonlinear analogue of the Li-Yau inequality for positive solutions of the normalized parabolic $p$-Laplacian equation \[ u_t = \Delta u + (p-2)|
abla u|^{-2}
abla^2u(
abla u,
abla u),\ \ \ 1<p<\infty, \] on a closed Riemannian manifold with nonnegative Ricci curvature, the equation being interpreted in the viscosity sense on the critical set of the solution. We also derive a sharp global Harnack inequality from the gradient estimate. The constant is best possible. Equality holds identically for an explicit self-similar solution in $\Rn$, and sharpness on closed manifolds follows by taking the limit along the flat tori $\mathbb R^n/(L\mathbb Z)^n$ as $L 	o \infty$. The proof rests on an exact Bochner-type identity for a family of uniformly parabolic approximating flows. We choose the first-order term separately from the second-order regularization so that the maximum principle yields the sharp constant, uniformly in the regularization parameter and without any assumption on the critical set of the solution. Using this Bochner identity with a modified Li-Yau functional, we extend the estimate to closed manifolds with $\operatorname{Ric} \ge -\kappa$.

item.title: Sharp degree bound for rational proper maps from $\mathbb B^2$ to $\mathbb B^4$
item.description: arXiv:2609.15698v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every rational proper holomorphic map from $\mathbb{B}^2$ to $\mathbb{B}^4$ has degree at most $5$, confirming D'Angelo's conjecture in this case. This sharp bound follows from Meylan's degree estimates and an intersection-theoretic argument ruling out degree $6$.
item.dc:creator: Tianzhi Hu, Mai Shi, Pingsan Yuan

item.title: A sharp two-disk bound for the second positive Neumann eigenvalue under a curvature upper bound
item.description: arXiv:2609.26609v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove the sharp two-disk comparison conjectured by Langford and Laugesen for the second positive Neumann eigenvalue under an upper Gaussian-curvature bound, and strengthen it to a shifted reciprocal inequality. Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{C}$ be bounded, simply connected and Lipschitz, with $g=\omega|dz|^2$, where $\omega$ is continuous and positive on $\overline{\Omega}$ and $\Delta\log\omega+2K\omega\ge0$ in distributions. Write $A=|\Omega|_g$ and enumerate the spectrum by $0=\lambda_0<\lambda_1\le\lambda_2\le\cdots$. If $KA<4\pi$ when $K>0$, then $\frac{1}{\lambda_2}+\frac{1}{\lambda_3}>\frac{2}{\lambda_1(D_K(A/2))}$ and $\lambda_2<\lambda_1(D_K(A/2))$, where $D_K(A/2)$ is the constant-curvature disk of area $A/2$. The same conclusions hold for disk-type Lipschitz domains in smooth surfaces. In the subcritical regime, both bounds are sharp, as witnessed by an extremizing sequence of smooth connected domains of exact area and curvature whose Neumann eigenvalues converge, at every fixed index, to those of two disjoint equal model disks. At $KA=4\pi$ we obtain the sharp non-strict bounds $\lambda_2\le2K$ and $\lambda_2^{-1}+\lambda_3^{-1}\ge K^{-1}$. The proof combines two-pole Green coordinates, positive-kernel comparison, and simultaneous centering. We also establish a global quadratic deficit for the model area split.
item.dc:creator: Meiqi Liu, Zhouyu Long, Wenming Zou

item.title: Codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphisms
item.description: arXiv:2609.37695v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every codimension-one holomorphic Anosov diffeomorphism of a compact connected complex manifold is biholomorphically conjugate to a hyperbolic automorphism of a complex torus. This verifies a conjecture of Ghys in the codimension-one case and, in particular, in complex dimension three.
item.dc:creator: Jiesong Zhang

item.title: Symplectic symmetries of a hypothetical exotic $CP^2$: a potential construction or a nonexistence proof
item.description: arXiv:2610.06746v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper is primarily concerned with the existence of a symplectic $4$-manifold, homeomorphic but not diffeomorphic to $CP^2$, which admits a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism. We reduced the existence of such an exotic $CP^2$ to a question in contact geometry. More concretely, we showed that there are precisely $12$ plumbed manifolds, each equipped with a canonical contact structure associated to the plumbing, such that an exotic $CP^2$ with a nontrivial finite order symplectomorphism exists if and only if one of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds admits a certain specific symplectic filling. As the main technical result, we completely determined the order and local representations of a pseudofree symplectic $Z_p$-action for an odd prime $p$ on a rational homology $CP^2$ with positive canonical class. Our result suggests that potentially, there are symplectic $Z_p$-actions which are not a finite automorphism of a fake projective plane. Moreover, we introduced a construction, which, under the minimal assumptions on the symplectic fillings of the $12$ contact plumbed manifolds, produces a symplectic $4$-manifold on the Bogomolov-Miyaoka-Yau line via a reverse-engineering process.
item.dc:creator: Weimin Chen

item.title: Sharp commutator bounds on complex simple Lie algebras: the B\"ottcher--Wenzel inequality and the comass of the Cartan $3$-form
item.description: arXiv:2610.11800v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For a complex simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak{g}$ with compact conjugation $\tau$, Killing form $B$, and Hermitian form $H(x, y) = -B(x, \tau y)$, it is shown that $H([x,y],[x,y]) \leq (h^{\vee})^{-1}H(x,x)H(y,y)$, where $h^{\vee}$ is the dual Coxeter number, with equality exactly for $H$-orthogonal pairs in $\tau$-stable long-root subalgebras isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{C})$. Equivalently, the comass of the Cartan $3$-form with respect to $H$ equals its comass on the compact real form: the spectral norm of the Cartan $3$-form does not increase under complexification. For the Frobenius norm on the image of a representation of Dynkin index $\ell$ the optimal constant is $2/\ell$; this contains the B\"ottcher--Wenzel and Bloch--Iserles inequalities, extends the latter to complex skew-symmetric matrices, and improves them substantially for the exceptional Lie algebras of types $F_{4}$, $E_{6}$, $E_{7}$, and $E_{8}$. The proof uses the Nahm algebra of $\mathfrak{g}$ with the conjugation induced by $\tau$: critical points of the relevant function correspond to $\tau$-twisted idempotents, and its Hessian is governed by $\tau$-twisted multiplication operators, whose anticommutation with multiplication by $i$ turns the one-sided second order condition at a maximum into a two-sided spectral bound. Subalgebras isomorphic to $\mathfrak{sl}(2, \mathbb{C})$ of Dynkin index $j$ give critical points with critical value $1/(jh^{\vee})$, whose Morse indices are computed, and the set of maximum points is a nondegenerate critical manifold. Geometrically, the maximal complex sectional curvature of a compact simple Lie group equals its maximal sectional curvature.
item.dc:creator: Daniel J. F. Fox

item.title: Rational curves on toroidal compactifications of Picard modular varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.12071v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: It was known that the canonical bundle of a smooth toroidal compactification of a noncompact finite-volume ball quotient is nef in dimension $n\geq3$ and ample in dimension $n\geq6$. We prove that the canonical bundle is ample in dimension $n\geq4$ and show that this dimension bound is sharp. We construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular threefolds whose smooth projective toroidal compactifications have non-ample canonical bundle. Each compactification contains a smooth rational curve meeting the interior and having canonical degree zero. More generally, in every dimension $n\geq2$, we construct infinitely many pairwise noncommensurable noncompact Picard modular varieties whose smooth toroidal compactifications contain smooth rational curves meeting the interior. In particular, such curves persist in arbitrarily high dimension, even when the canonical bundle is ample.
item.dc:creator: Soheil Memariansorkhabi, Sai-Kee Yeung

item.title: Hyperquiver varieties
item.description: arXiv:2610.12261v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We discuss the recently introduced concept of hyperquivers, due to Muller, Nanda, and Seigal, from the point of view of K\"ahler and hyperk\"ahler quotients. In particular, we show that the K\"ahler hyperquiver variety ${\mathcal M}$, corresponding to a hyperquiver with a single hyperedge, is a projective variety isomorphic to the geometric quotient of the space of tensors with maximal multilinear rank. Moreover, the hyperk\"ahler hyperquiver variety corresponding to doubling of this hyperquiver can be identified with the linear scheme corresponding to the sheaf of reflexive $1$-forms on ${\mathcal M}$.
item.dc:creator: Roger Bielawski
